name: Fallout TTRPG 2.1 - Fuse's Rewrite
author: Fuse (rules), GabrielGugg (package)
description: Fuse's Rewrite of Arcane Arcade's Fallout TTRPG 2.1, as an extension: core rules, races and variants (with Feral Levels), backgrounds, traits, perks, weapons, explosives, ammunition, armor, power armor, consumables, addictions, gear, materials and junk. Statblocks and the experimental documents are not included. Rules by Fuse; package by GabrielGugg. Needs StatForge 1.25.0 or later.

fields.description:
The Barter skill measures your expertise in trade. Whether that be with merchants when trading valuables or with powerful figures to discuss terms. Barter encompasses all manner of exchange, this for that. The higher your Barter skill, the more convincing you are when it comes to sweetening your deals.

You can also use this skill with a unique ability called Discount. When you purchase an item from a merchant with any kind of currency, you can use your Discount ability to gain a percentage discount equal to your Barter skill bonus. This discount has a maximum of 85% off. Once you use the Discount ability, you cannot use it again until you take a long rest.

See more about Bartering mechanics in the Bartering section.

The Breach skill measures your ability to open locks, hack computers, disarm traps, or anything that lets you get to places you’re not supposed to. You can pick locks at any time without any sort of equipment, however certain items can make lockpicking easier. Whenever you make a Breach check, you can re-roll the check a number of times equal to your Luck modifier. When you are trying to pick locks, you will use your Perception modifier for your Breach skill (up to Overseer’s discretion).

You can pick locks at any time without any sort of equipment, however certain items can make lockpicking easier. Whenever you make a Breach check, you can re-roll the check a number of times equal to your Luck modifier. When you are trying to hack computers, you will use your Intelligence modifier for your Breach skill (up to Overseer’s discretion).

fields.description:
The Crafting skill measures your knowledge of schematics to repair and craft items. To craft most weapons, armor, mods, and upgrades, your Crafting skill must be greater than or equal to the listed requirement. If you do not meet the requirement, you can roll a Crafting skill check with the DC being 12 + the Crafting skill requirement. On a success you craft the items, on a failure you do not craft the items and you use half of your choice of the required materials. If an item has a level of Decay, you can use your Crafting skill to repair it and remove the level of Decay.

See more about Crafting mechanics in the Crafting and Repair section.

The Energy Weapons skill measures your expertise in the use of technological weapons that shoot powerful lasers, flash arcs of electricity, fire superheated bolts of plasma, and even launch ammo with electromagnetic coils to accelerate projectiles at extreme velocities. When you make an attack roll with an Energy Weapon, you add your Energy Weapons skill modifier to the attack roll. When you hit with an Energy Weapon, you add your Perception modifier to the damage roll.

The Explosives skill measures your know-how in arming, disarming, and overall handling of any explosive device. Whether that be a fragmentation grenade, C-4 explosive, molotov cocktail, plasma grenade, or smoke bomb.

When you use your AP to arm and throw an explosive, roll a d20 and add your Explosives skill modifier. If the total is a 1, the explosive detonates immediately before you throw it. If the total is a 2 or 3, the explosive is thrown half the distance and detonates at the start of your next turn. If the total is between 3 and 14, the explosive detonates at the start of your next turn. If the result is a 15 or higher, the explosive detonates at the end of your turn

When you use your AP to throw an explosive that has already been armed, roll an Explosives check. If the result is a 12 or below, the explosive is not thrown and explodes immediately. If the result is above an 13, the explosive detonates at the end of your turn.

The Guns skill measures your ability to wield and shoot all manner of firearms. From revolvers, to snipers rifles, to miniguns. When you make an attack roll with a handgun, rifle, SMG, shotgun, or heavy weapon, you add your Guns skill bonus to the attack roll. When you hit with a ranged attack, you add your Agility modifier to the damage roll.

The Intimidation skill measures how physically daunting you are, your ability to frighten others, or even make them re-evaluate confronting you. You can optionally choose for your Intimidation skill to be modified by your Strength modifier instead of Charisma. Depending on how you are trying to intimidate someone, you may be asked to use the Strength or Charisma modifiers for an Intimidation check.

The Intimidation skill measures how threatening you can be, your ability to frighten others, or even make them re-evaluate confronting you. You can optionally choose for your Intimidation skill to be modified by your Strength modifier instead of Charisma. Depending on how you are trying to intimidate someone, you may be asked to use the Strength or Charisma modifiers for an Intimidation check.

fields.description:
The Medicine skill measures your aptitude for accessing symptoms and properly treating them with care while under pressure.

If you are within 5 ft. of a creature with the Bleeding condition, you can spend 6 AP to mend to their wound, requiring x1 cloth junk item and passing a DC 15 Medicine skill check to remove a level of Bleeding.

If another creature is Dying and has not failed all of their Death Saves, you can spend 6 AP to make a Medicine check with a DC equal to 10 + (their failed Death Saves - their successful Death Saves). On a success, the creature gains 1 HP and loses the Dying condition.

You can optionally choose for your Medicine skill to be modified by your Intelligence modifier instead of Perception. Depending on how you are trying to heal, you may be asked to use the Perception or Intelligence modifiers.

The Medicine skill measures your knowledge of anatomy, physiology, and methods to keep creatures alive.

Knowledge of Medicine also allows you to craft chems. To craft most chem recipes, your Medicine skill must be greater than or equal to its requirement. This uses your Intelligence modifier, not your Perception modifier, for the Medicine skill bonus.

If you are within 5 ft. of a creature with the Bleeding condition, you can spend 6 AP to mend to their wound, requiring x1 cloth junk item and passing a DC 15 Medicine skill check to remove a level of Bleeding.

If another creature is Dying and has not failed all of their Death Saves, you can spend 6 AP to make a Medicine check with a DC equal to 10 + (their failed Death Saves - their successful Death Saves). On a success, the creature gains 1 HP and loses the Dying condition.

You can optionally choose for your Medicine skill to be modified by your Perception modifier instead of Intelligence. Depending on how you are trying to heal, you may be asked to use the Perception or Intelligence modifiers.

fields.description: The Melee Weapons skill measures your ability to chop, stab, or bludgeon with weapons such as knives, boards, 9-irons, or even chainsaws. When you make an attack roll with a Melee Weapon, you add your Melee Weapons skill bonus to the attack roll. When you hit with a Melee Weapon attack, you add your Strength modifier to the damage roll.

The Science skill measures your knowledge and deductive reasoning for all kinds of studies. Biology, historiography, cosmology, chemistry, geology, etc.. You can use the Science skill to craft advanced technology and upgrades. If your character ever encounters something mysterious, you can make a Science skill check to deduce the reasoning. Alternatively, if your Overseer allows it, you can ask the Overseer a question about a specific subject that you may not know the answer to, but your character might. On a successful roll you may learn the information.

The Sneak skill measures your ability to remain quiet or inconspicuous.

On your turn you can spend 6 AP to Hide. When you Hide, you roll a Sneak skill check. If you have cover against any creatures and your Sneak skill check total is greater than their Passive Sense, then you are hidden from them and they cannot see you. If you attack a creature who you are hidden from, you gain advantage on the attack roll. If you hit, the damage from the attack is dealt directly to the target’s HP, ignoring any SP. If you attack with an unsilenced ranged weapon, your position is revealed and you are no longer Hidden.

See more about Stealth mechanics in the Stealth section.

The Speech skill measures your ability to communicate and to read others. Speech encompasses your ability to persuade, dissuade, convince, or deceive. Knowledge of language, oratory, and expression also falls under Speech. You can use the Speech skill to convince non-player characters to agree with you, perform a favor for you, or even risk their life for you (at Overseer’s discretion). You can also use Speech to tell a convincing lie, read the intentions of someone who may have ill-intent towards you, or to communicate non-verbally.

The Survival skill measures a mixture of your adaptation, knowledge of the land, ability to hunt, and expertise in cuisine. You can use your Survival skill to track creatures, craft food and drinks, and learn about creatures. When crafting most food and drink recipes, your Survival skill modifier must be greater than or equal to the listed requirement. Additionally, learning more about a creature’s habits, type, or physical abilities might require a Survival check (at Overseer’s discretion).

Archery Weapons use the Survival skill to attack, and Endurance for damage.

The Unarmed skill measures your ability to punch, strike, wrestle, kick, elbow, knee, or grapple other creatures. When you make an Unarmed attack roll, you add your Unarmed skill bonus to the attack roll. When you hit with an Unarmed attack, you add your Strength modifier to the damage roll. Unarmed attacks can be non-lethal.

entity.name: Combat Sequence bonus
entity.description: When combat begins, every creature rolls Combat Sequence and adds its Perception modifier. Traits and perks that change it are already added here.

fields.description: Your Healing Rate is equal to (your level + your Endurance score) / 2, to a minimum of 1. It is how many HP you gain from healing.

Manual: it depends on the whole party. Your Party Nerve bonus is equal to every player character’s Charisma modifier added together, then halved (rounded down). It is added to your Death Saves, and at the start of combat each player gains temporary SP equal to it.
Manual: it depends on the whole party. Group Sneak is every player’s Sneak skill modifier added together, divided by the number of players.
All your skills gain a bonus equal to half your Luck modifier (rounded down). If your Luck has a negative modifier, all your skill bonuses are reduced by 1 regardless of your modifier.

fields.description: At every level except 5th, 9th, 13th, 17th, 21st, 25th, and 29th, you gain 1 perk point. Spend it on a perk you meet the requirements for, or to increase one of your ability scores by 1.

For every level of Hunger you have, your d20 rolls are reduced by 1. If you do not eat food for 24 hours, you gain a level of Hunger. You can remove a level of Hunger by eating food. If you gain 10 levels of Hunger, you die.

For every level of Dehydration you have, your d20 rolls are reduced by 1. If you do not drink for 24 hours, you gain a level of Dehydration. You can remove a level of Dehydration by drinking something. If you gain 10 levels of Dehydration, you die.

For every level of Fatigue you have, your d20 rolls are reduced by 1. You lose a level of Fatigue at the end of each turn in combat, and you lose all levels of Fatigue when you rest. If you gain 10 levels of Fatigue, you fall Unconscious.

For every level of Exhaustion you have, your d20 rolls are reduced by 1. If you do not rest for 24 hours, you gain a level of Exhaustion. You can remove a level of Exhaustion by resting. When you reach 5 levels of Exhaustion, it costs 2 AP to move 5 ft. and you can only move a maximum of 30 ft. on your turn. If you gain 10 levels of Exhaustion, you die.

For every level of Radiation you have, your d20 rolls are reduced by 1. When you gain a level of Radiation, you take 1d4 radiation damage to your HP and must make a Mutation check. If you reach 10 levels of Radiation or radiation damage brings you to 0 HP, you die. Optionally, you can make a DC 20 Luck check. On a success, you return to 1 HP as a Ghoul. If you fail by more than 5, you return as a Feral Ghoul.

Whenever you roll a d20 (besides Luck), the result is decreased by 1 for every level of Hypothermia you have. Additionally, your maximum AP is decreased by a number equal to half your levels of Hypothermia, rounded down. When you gain your 10th level of Hypothermia, you die.

Whenever you roll a d20 (besides Luck), the result is decreased by 1 for every level of Overheating you have. Additionally, your maximum AP is decreased by a number equal to half your levels of Overheating, rounded down. When you gain your 10th level of Overheating, you die.

For every level of Bleeding a creature has, it takes damage to their HP equal to half their Healing Rate at the start of their turn. A creature with the Dying condition will automatically fail a Death Save if they have this condition on their turn. If a creature with Bleeding is healed, they do not gain HP and instead remove two levels of Bleeding.

For every level of Short Circuit a robot has, it takes 1d6 electricity damage to their HP and their maximum AP is reduced by 1 at the start of their turn. If a Short Circuiting robot becomes wet, their levels of Short Circuit double. A robot loses all levels of Short Circuit if they begin Dying or are healed to full HP. A robot can also spend 6 AP to re-route and reset their circuit, removing one level of Short Circuit.

entity.name: Feral Levels
entity.description: Ghouls only. Whenever you make a skill check, the result is decreased by your Feral Levels (not ability checks or attack rolls). When a trigger occurs, make a Feral Check (Intelligence or Luck, DC by event + your Feral Levels); on a failure you gain a Feral Level. At 10 Feral Levels (8 for Ancient Ghouls) you become feral and are controlled by the Overseer. Vials remove 1 Feral Level.

fields.description:
Humans are the dominant species of Earth. In the post–apocalyptic age, "human" is more specifically used to denote those that have been more-or-less unaffected by radiation as opposed to mutants like ghouls and super mutants, even though said mutant types originate from humans.

Despite the existence of various mutations, humans are still the most common humanoid creatures on Earth. Post-nuclear humans, as a direct result of the radiation and exposition to the Forced Evolutionary Virus and some other biochemical agents released into the environment during and after the Great War, exhibit more diversity, primarily in genetic structure. The aforementioned factors have resulted in an increased rate of mutations in humans, although very few of these result in phenotypic changes. Most of these changes are non-lethal, non-damaging variations in the human DNA that simply increase the gene pool variety. Also, humans with minor mutations, like additional toes, skin lesions due to TDC infection, permanent red eyes, permanent varicose veins, or complete lack of hair are still considered to be humans.

Age. Humans reach adulthood in their late teens and generally live less than a century, though it’s rare for a person to live that long in the wasteland.

Size. Humans vary wildly in height and build, your size is Medium or Small.

Tenacity. When you roll Death Saves, you can fail 4 times before you die, rather than 3.

Unevolved. You can gain levels of Radiation when in radioactive areas or when dealing with radioactive material, such as Irradiated food or creatures.

effects.text: Feral Levels (ghouls only)

fields.description:
Ghouls are mutated humans affected by the phenomenon of ghoulification. Despite their zombie-like appearance, the flesh of ghouls is not actually rotten. Intense and prolonged radiation has ravaged their skin, much of their flesh, and in some cases many of their ligaments. Despite their infertility and in some cases mental deterioration, they have greatly extended overall lifespans and are immune to (and sometimes even healed by) background radiation and/or nuclear fallout.

Age. Ghouls are nearly immortal, their lifespan is unknown. Some Ghouls have survived from even before the Great War over 200 years ago.

Size. Ghouls vary widely in height and build, your size is Medium or Small.

Evolution. You cannot gain levels of Radiation or Rads and are immune to radiation damage.

Resilient Anatomy. You are resistant to poison damage, you take half as much damage from the Bleeding condition, and you have advantage on checks to resist gaining Diseases. However, you gain half as much SP (rounded down) when consuming food, drinks or chems, you gain half as much HP (rounded down) from Stimpaks, and you cannot gain any HP from Healing Powder.

Grasp On Humanity. Radiation takes a toll on one’s mind, and every ghoul constantly struggles against the threat of becoming feral. You have Feral Levels, a representation of how fractured and damaged your mind is. As you gain more Feral Levels, you become more irritable, forgettable, and may begin suffering from seizures and tremors. These levels can be gained based on certain events or triggers, including gameplay triggers, as listed in the table below, and narrative triggers, as determined by the Overseer.

When one of these triggers occurs, you must make a Feral Check, which is an Intelligence or Luck ability check. The DC of this check is dependent on the event that triggered it + your current Feral Levels. For narrative triggers, the Overseer can determine the DC. On a failure, your mind fractures and you gain a Feral Level. On a success, you maintain your composure and nothing happens.

Whenever you make a skill check, the result is decreased by a number equal to your Feral Levels. This does not include ability checks or attack rolls. If you reach 10 Feral Levels, your character becomes feral and is now controlled by the Overseer.

This table defines the gameplay events that trigger a Feral Check. Each event has its own base DC for the Feral Check, which has your current number of Feral Levels added to it, as well as additional effects listed in the Notes column.

Gameplay Event — Feral Check DC — Notes

Reaching 0 HP — *Automatic Failure* — Feral Roll immediately fails.

Taking a Severe Injury — 14 — Feral Roll has disadvantage.

Seeing a party member reach 0 HP — 10 — While a party member is Dying, any Feral Rolls you make are decreased by 1.

Taking a critical hit — 8

Gaining a level of Hunger, Dehydration, or Exhaustion. — 5

Critically failing a roll or attack — 5

Taking any damage to your HP — *Equal to half of damage taken (rounded up), to a max of 12.*

Leveling up — *Equal to half your level (rounded up)*

If you are under the effect of a chem, you have advantage on any Feral Check. A rare but powerful medicine exists, known only as Vials, that can fully remove 1 Feral Level upon using it. Certain perks and abilities will also grant you bonuses and additional ways to deal with your Feral Levels.

fields.description:
Synth (short for synthetic humanoids, also called androids or artificial humans) is a common term used to refer to biological and mechanical robots manufactured within the Institute laboratories. Synths, in extremely rare cases, can escape the clutches of the Institute and live their own lives, sometimes even having their memory erased and filled with new ones to live out their lives.

Gen-2 Synths, however, are a different story. They are much more clearly androids, with plastic-like skin, exposed insides, and metal pieces. Gen-2s still possess limited A.I. and superficially resemble a mannequin more than a human.

Age. Synths can live hundreds of years before their inorganic materials begin to corrode and their programming deteriorates. However, a Synth who keeps consistent repairs is nigh immortal.

Size. Synths are built to resemble humans, thus your size is Medium.

Inorganic Body. You cannot gain Radiation levels or Rads and you are immune to radiation damage. Additionally, you are immune to poison damage and the Bleeding condition, however you can gain levels of Short Circuit. You gain no effects from Medicine, Chems, Drinks or Food, but you can use Robot Repair Kits and Robot Overclock Programs. You have no need to breathe, sleep, eat, or drink, and you cannot gain Diseases.

Severed Limbs. Luckily for Synths, reattaching limbs is commonplace when they break or fall off. If any of your limbs (other than your head) are severed, you do not go into Shock and they can be reattached with 2 steel and 3 circuitry materials. When you or a creature reattaches a limb, it takes a number of minutes equal to 10 - their or your Crafting skill modifier. If the amount of time is reduced to 0, it takes 6 AP to reattach the limb instead.

Electronic Components. You are weak to Electricity damage, but you count as a Robot for any perk requirements. You cannot, however, gain Integrated Weapons.

Brittle Body. When you take damage to your HP from a Targeted Attack, you gain 2 limb conditions instead of 1.

fields.description:
A robot is a machine that is capable of autonomously completing tasks. Depending upon the robot, these tasks may be simple or complex and may require little human intervention or complete oversight. Robots had been constructed by pre-War society to fill all niches and occupations. From general-purpose utility droids to full-fledged military battle machines, robots could be found in almost any environment and function.

Age. Robots can live hundreds of years before their inorganic materials begin to corrode and their programming deteriorates. However, a Robot who keeps consistent repairs is nigh immortal.

Size. Most robots were built to the same scale as humans, though they vary slightly depending on the type of robot. Regardless, your size is Medium.

Inorganic Body. You cannot gain Radiation levels or Rads and you are immune to radiation damage, poison damage and the Bleeding condition, however you can now gain levels of Short Circuit. You gain no effects from medicine, chems, drinks or food, but you can use Robot Repair Kits and Robot Overclock Programs. You have no need to breathe, sleep, eat, or drink, and you cannot gain Diseases.

Additionally, unless otherwise stated, you are immune to psychic damage.

Insulated. Your internals are insulated against the cold, however they are vulnerable to high heat. When in Extreme Cold environments, you take twice as long to gain any levels of Hypothermia. However, when in Extreme Heat environments, you gain twice as many levels of Overheating.

Severed Limbs. Luckily for most robots, reattaching limbs is commonplace when they break or fall off. If any of your limbs are severed, you do not go into shock and they can be reattached with 3 steel and 1 circuitry junk item. When you or a creature reattaches a limb, it takes a number of minutes equal to 10 - their or your Crafting skill modifier. If the amount of time is reduced to 0, it takes 6 AP to reattach the limb instead.

Integrated Weapons. Robots can either come with or be modified to have weapons integrated into their arms. Integrated Weapons cost no AP to draw or stow, only require one hand to use, and unless otherwise specified, the arm retains the use of a hand. Integrated Weapons that come built-in to the robot have no Carry Load or Strength Requirement. These Integrated Weapons can be upgraded and modified just like any other weapon, however they can also gain levels of Decay like any other weapon. Additionally, they cannot be detached from you unless the arm that the tool or weapon is attached to is severed.

Armor. You can use armor just as any other race would, however you cannot wear Power Armor.

Electronic Components. You are weak to Electricity damage.

Robot Sub-Type. There are 6 different robot variants available. You must choose one from the list below.

fields.description:
Super mutants are genetically enhanced humans who were created to be superior in every way to a typical human. Originally planned to be super soldiers, the first Super mutants were created by exposure to the Forced Evolutionary Virus II from the vats of the Mariposa Military Base in California. Other strains of Super mutants are found throughout the wasteland created from various sources, often varying in size and intelligence. Regardless of their origin, all Super mutants were created by way of the Forced Evolutionary Virus having mutated from humans.

People who were turned into mutants via would have their skin turn a shade of green, yellow, or olive with their entire body growing huge with more muscle mass being added by the Virus. But those who were turned into mutants had only fleeting memories of their human lives. They could not breed, as the FEV turned them sterile, thus limiting the generations of mutants. A strain of mutants known as nightkin had their skin change to a gray-purple color after long exposure to stealth boys.

Age. Super mutants are nearly immortal, their lifespan is unknown. Some have lived for hundreds of years.

Size. Super mutants rarely vary in height and build, but they can range from 7 to 9 ft. in height. Your size is Medium.

Evolution. You cannot gain levels of Radiation and you are immune to radiation damage. Additionally, you gain no Rads from consuming food or water. You are also immune to gaining Diseases.

Armor and Weapons. Due to your size, you cannot use Power Armor unless it has been specifically modded to fit your larger body.

Superior Strength. Due to your increased mass in muscle, your Strength score increases by 1 and cannot be lower than 6. Additionally your Carry Load is increased by 40.

*(If your Strength score is lower than 6 after applying the bonus, you must lower one or more abilities to get your Strength to at least 6.)*

Mass Exertion. You need a lot more food and water to keep your body running smoothly. You need twice as much food and water every day, and when you would normally take 1 level of Hunger or Dehydration, you instead take 2 levels. However, you ignore the Cannibalistic, Diseased, and Irradiated food properties.

Bulky. Super mutants have many advantages, but precision does not come easy. Whenever your weapons or armor would gain a level of Decay, they instead take 2 levels of Decay.
