fields.description:
Requirement: Robot, Not Gen-2 Synth

You can choose any 2 weapons to become Integrated Weapons, so long as you have the caps to purchase them, the materials to craft them, or you have the weapons in your inventory. The weapons you choose have their Carry Load halved, they cost no AP to equip or stow, and they cannot be detached from you unless the arm is severed. The chosen weapons retain all properties.

You can only have one Integrated Weapon per arm. If you already have an Integrated Weapon in one of your arms, you can choose to replace it with a new weapon.

effects.text: Hardware Upgrade: You can choose any 2 weapons to become Integrated Weapons, so long as you have the caps to purchase them, the materials to craft them, or you have the weapons in your inventory. The weapons you choose have their Carry Load halved, they cost no AP to equip or stow, and they cannot be detached from you unless the arm is severed. The chosen weapons retain all properties.

fields.description:
Requirement: Robot, Level 8

Can be taken 3 times.

Your AC and DT increase by 1.

Each rank of this perk increases the AC and DT bonus by 1.

Requirement: Endurance 8

You are immune to all limb conditions that are not Severe Injuries, and whenever you take damage to your HP from a Targeted Attack to your legs or arms, the damage is halved.

effects.text: Adamantium Skeleton: You are immune to all limb conditions that are not Severe Injuries, and whenever you take damage to your HP from a Targeted Attack to your legs or arms, the damage is halved.

fields.description:
Requirement: Agility 6

You never set off placed explosives or traps located on the floor. Additionally, you can ignore the negative effects of the Slippery Surface environmental hazard.

effects.text: Light Step: You never set off placed explosives or traps located on the floor. Additionally, you can ignore the negative effects of the Slippery Surface environmental hazard.

fields.description:
Requirement: Robot, Level 5

You can spend 6 AP on your turn to heal a number of SP equal to double your Healing Rate. You can only heal this way once before needing to take a long rest.

effects.text: Pump the Coolant: You can spend 6 AP on your turn to heal a number of SP equal to double your Healing Rate. You can only heal this way once before needing to take a long rest.

fields.description:
Requirement: Super Mutant

You can spend 6 AP on your turn to heal a number of HP equal to your Healing Rate. You can only heal this way once before needing to take a Long Rest.

effects.text: Reinforced Recovery: You can spend 6 AP on your turn to heal a number of HP equal to your Healing Rate. You can only heal this way once before needing to take a Long Rest.

fields.description:
Requirement: Super Mutant

You’ve gotten used to your bulky hands. When crafting or repairing an item, the DC is decreased by 5.

effects.text: Fine-Toothed Giant: You’ve gotten used to your bulky hands. When crafting or repairing an item, the DC is decreased by 5.

fields.description:
Requirement: Super Mutant

You no longer require double the amount of water each day to avoid Dehydration. Additionally, Dirty Water now has the Hydrating property for you.

effects.text: Wasteland Camel: You no longer require double the amount of water each day to avoid Dehydration. Additionally, Dirty Water now has the Hydrating property for you.

fields.description:
Requirement: Super Mutant, Level 5

Super Mutants will not target you unless you are the only hostile target within 60 ft.. Additionally, you can spend 3 AP on your turn and choose one Super Mutant within 60 ft. of you to learn that Super Mutant’s ability scores.

effects.text: No Gods, No Masters: Super Mutants will not target you unless you are the only hostile target within 60 ft.. Additionally, you can spend 3 AP on your turn and choose one Super Mutant within 60 ft. of you to learn that Super Mutant’s ability scores.

fields.description:
Requirement: Super Mutant, Level 5

Your DT increases by 1. Additionally, if you end your turn with at least 6 AP, whenever you take damage to your HP, you can spend that 6 AP as a reaction to reduce the damage by half (rounded down).

effects.text: Feel No Wounds: Your DT increases by 1. Additionally, if you end your turn with at least 6 AP, whenever you take damage to your HP, you can spend that 6 AP as a reaction to reduce the damage by half (rounded down).

fields.description:
Requirement: Super Mutant, Level 10

Your AC increases by 1, your DT increases by 1, and your HP and SP increases by a number equal to your level. Additionally, choose one damage type to become resistant to.

effects.text: Evolution: Your AC increases by 1, your DT increases by 1, and your HP and SP increases by a number equal to your level. Additionally, choose one damage type to become resistant to.

entity.name: Archer
entity.description:
Can be taken 3 times.

Whenever you make an attack or damage roll with an Archery Weapon, add 2 to the result.

Each rank of this perk increases the modifier by 1.

effects.text: Archer: Whenever you make an attack or damage roll with an Archery Weapon, add 2 to the result.

entity.name: Low-Tech Warfare
entity.description: Add insult to injury! When you deal damage with a Targeted Attack with an Archery Weapon against Robot enemies, you deal full damage instead of half damage. Additionally, if you deal damage to the Defense Points of a target wearing Power Armor, you deal twice as much damage.

effects.text: Low-Tech Warfare: Add insult to injury! When you deal damage with a Targeted Attack with an Archery Weapon against Robot enemies, you deal full damage instead of half damage. Additionally, if you deal damage to the Defense Points of a target wearing Power Armor, you deal twice as much damage.

entity.name: Groovy
entity.description:
Requirement: Missing Hand

Can be repeated for each missing hand.

You replace your missing hand with a Melee Weapon of your choice, though you must either have the weapon in your inventory or the crafting materials to make it. The weapon no longer costs AP to stow or equip and can only be removed from you if your hand is removed once again. You gain advantage on attack rolls when using this weapon.

(Note: Using this perk means that hand is no longer eligible for the Adaptive Reflexes perk.)

effects.text: Groovy: Can be repeated for each missing hand.

entity.name: Starched Genes
entity.description:
Requirement: Human, Level 5

When you fail a Mutation check, you can optionally choose to not gain any mutations. Additionally, when removing levels of Radiation, you can optionally choose to not remove any mutations.

effects.text: Starched Genes: When you fail a Mutation check, you can optionally choose to not gain any mutations. Additionally, when removing levels of Radiation, you can optionally choose to not remove any mutations.

entity.name: Restful Meditations
entity.description:
Requirement: Ghoul

You’ve learned how to put your mind at ease while resting. When you take a Long Rest, you can remove 1 Feral Level.

effects.text: Restful Meditations: You’ve learned how to put your mind at ease while resting. When you take a Long Rest, you can remove 1 Feral Level.

entity.name: Feral Rage
entity.description:
Requirement: Ghoul, Strength 7

For every Feral Level you have, you deal an additional +1 damage on your Melee or Unarmed attack rolls.

effects.text: Feral Rage: For every Feral Level you have, you deal an additional +1 damage on your Melee or Unarmed attack rolls.

entity.name: Chem Diet
entity.description:
Requirement: Ghoul, Endurance 7

Whenever you make a Feral Check while under the effect of a chem, the roll is increased by +2.

effects.text: Chem Diet: Whenever you make a Feral Check while under the effect of a chem, the roll is increased by +2.

entity.name: Moral Support
entity.description:
Requirement: Ghoul, Charisma 5

Whenever you make a Feral Check, you can add your Party Nerve to the roll in addition to your INT/LCK.

effects.text: Moral Support: Whenever you make a Feral Check, you can add your Party Nerve to the roll in addition to your INT/LCK.

entity.name: Feral Presence
entity.description:
Requirement: Ghoul, Charisma 6

While you have any Feral Levels, you can choose to spend 6 AP to attempt to Frighten a creature you can see. The creature must make an Endurance ability check with a DC equal to 8 + your Feral Levels. On a failure, they are Frightened of you for a number of rounds equal to 4 - the creature’s END modifier, to a minimum of 1.

effects.text: Feral Presence: While you have any Feral Levels, you can choose to spend 6 AP to attempt to Frighten a creature you can see. The creature must make an Endurance ability check with a DC equal to 8 + your Feral Levels. On a failure, they are Frightened of you for a number of rounds equal to 4 - the creature’s END modifier, to a minimum of 1.

entity.name: EMP Shield
entity.description:
Requirement: Robot, Level 3

You are no longer weak to Electricity damage.

effects.text: EMP Shield: You are no longer weak to Electricity damage.

entity.name: Slugger
entity.description:
Requirement: Strength 5

Batter up! If you have a Blunt Melee Weapon with the Two Handed property equipped and you make a Thrown Explosive attack, you can choose to add half your Melee Weapons skill modifier (rounded down) to the Explosives skill check, in addition to your Explosives skill modifier. Additionally, the range of the Thrown Explosive is doubled.

effects.text: Slugger: Batter up! If you have a Blunt Melee Weapon with the Two Handed property equipped and you make a Thrown Explosive attack, you can choose to add half your Melee Weapons skill modifier (rounded down) to the Explosives skill check, in addition to your Explosives skill modifier. Additionally, the range of the Thrown Explosive is doubled.

entity.name: Road Rage
entity.description:
Requirement: Strength 5

When you are driving a Vehicle and crash into a creature, vehicle, or obstacle, any impact damage they take is doubled.

effects.text: Road Rage: When you are driving a Vehicle and crash into a creature, vehicle, or obstacle, any impact damage they take is doubled.

entity.name: Hit and Run
entity.description:
Requirement: Strength 7

When you make an attack with a Melee Weapon, Unarmed Weapon, or Unarmed Strike while in a moving Vehicle, any damage you deal is doubled.

effects.text: Hit and Run: When you make an attack with a Melee Weapon, Unarmed Weapon, or Unarmed Strike while in a moving Vehicle, any damage you deal is doubled.

entity.name: Lock and Load
entity.description:
Requirement: Strength 8

When reloading weapons that have the Slow Reload property, it only costs 6 AP instead of 10 AP.

effects.text: Lock and Load: When reloading weapons that have the Slow Reload property, it only costs 6 AP instead of 10 AP.

entity.name: Hack and Slash
entity.description:
Requirement: Strength 10

Every Melee Weapon is considered to have the Cleave property when you attack with it. If the weapon already has the Cleave property, it now has the Always Cleaves property. If the weapon already has Always Cleaves property, it can now target an additional creature.

effects.text: Hack and Slash: Every Melee Weapon is considered to have the Cleave property when you attack with it. If the weapon already has the Cleave property, it now has the Always Cleaves property. If the weapon already has Always Cleaves property, it can now target an additional creature.

entity.name: On A Dime
entity.description:
Requirement: Perception 5

When you are driving a Vehicle, if the vehicle would crash into an obstacle, it instead stops right before colliding. No damage is dealt to the vehicle or the passengers, and the vehicle does not gain a level of Decay.

effects.text: On A Dime: When you are driving a Vehicle, if the vehicle would crash into an obstacle, it instead stops right before colliding. No damage is dealt to the vehicle or the passengers, and the vehicle does not gain a level of Decay.

entity.name: Hawkeye
entity.description:
Requirement: Perception 6

When you damage an enemy with an attack beyond the short range of your Archery Weapon, you deal an additional 1d6 damage.

effects.text: Hawkeye: When you damage an enemy with an attack beyond the short range of your Archery Weapon, you deal an additional 1d6 damage.

entity.name: Bow Before Me
entity.description:
Requirement: Perception 7

When you deal damage to a creature’s HP with Archery Weapons, you ignore 2 DT.

effects.text: Bow Before Me: When you deal damage to a creature’s HP with Archery Weapons, you ignore 2 DT.

entity.name: Drive By
entity.description:
Requirement: Perception 7

When you attack with a ranged weapon from a moving Vehicle or Vertibird, your attack no longer has disadvantage and deals an additional +1d8 damage.

effects.text: Drive By: When you attack with a ranged weapon from a moving Vehicle or Vertibird, your attack no longer has disadvantage and deals an additional +1d8 damage.

entity.name: Oh No You Don’t
entity.description:
Requirement: Perception 8

When you deal damage to a fleeing target’s HP with an Archery Weapon, your attack acts as a critical hit and the enemy is knocked Prone.

effects.text: Oh No You Don’t: When you deal damage to a fleeing target’s HP with an Archery Weapon, your attack acts as a critical hit and the enemy is knocked Prone.

entity.name: Eagle Eye
entity.description:
Requirement: Perception 8

Can be taken 2 times.

When making a Targeted Attack with a Ranged Weapon, the weapon’s short range is increased by half (rounded down, to a maximum of the weapon’s long range).

At 2nd rank, the weapon’s short range is doubled when making a Targeted Attack (to a maximum of the weapon’s long range).

effects.text: Eagle Eye: When making a Targeted Attack with a Ranged Weapon, the weapon’s short range is increased by half (rounded down, to a maximum of the weapon’s long range).

entity.name: Adventurer Ender
entity.description:
Requirement: Perception 9

They used to be adventurers like you, but then they took an arrow to the knee. When you damage a target’s HP with a Targeted Attack to the Legs with an Archery Weapon, they automatically gain the Broken Leg injury.

effects.text: Adventurer Ender: They used to be adventurers like you, but then they took an arrow to the knee. When you damage a target’s HP with a Targeted Attack to the Legs with an Archery Weapon, they automatically gain the Broken Leg injury.

entity.name: Vaccinated
entity.description:
Requirement: Endurance 4, Able to gain Diseases

Can be taken 3 times.

At rank 1 of this perk, you have +2 to all Disease checks.

At rank 2 of this perk, you have advantage on all Disease checks.

At rank 3 of this perk, you are immune to Diseases.

effects.text: Vaccinated: At rank 1 of this perk, you have +2 to all Disease checks.

entity.name: One for the Road
entity.description:
Requirement: Endurance 5

When you are driving a Vehicle while under the effects of an alcoholic drink, any action related to driving costs 2 less AP (to a minimum of 1) and you have advantage on checks to maintain control of the vehicle.

effects.text: One for the Road: When you are driving a Vehicle while under the effects of an alcoholic drink, any action related to driving costs 2 less AP (to a minimum of 1) and you have advantage on checks to maintain control of the vehicle.

entity.name: Revenant
entity.description:
Requirement: Endurance 6

When you recover from the Dying condition, you gain advantage on your attack rolls and deal +2 damage when you hit for 2 turns.

effects.text: Revenant: When you recover from the Dying condition, you gain advantage on your attack rolls and deal +2 damage when you hit for 2 turns.

entity.name: Fender Bender
entity.description:
Requirement: Endurance 7

When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird, any damage dealt to the vehicle is halved.

effects.text: Fender Bender: When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird, any damage dealt to the vehicle is halved.

entity.name: Sizzling Style
entity.description:
Requirement: Endurance 9

When you are wearing armor that has at least one Rank 3 upgrade, you gain resistance to two damage types of your choice while wearing the armor.

effects.text: Sizzling Style: When you are wearing armor that has at least one Rank 3 upgrade, you gain resistance to two damage types of your choice while wearing the armor.

entity.name: Carpool
entity.description:
Requirement: Charisma 5

When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird, its Capacity is increased by a number equal to half your Charisma modifier (rounded down).

effects.text: Carpool: When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird, its Capacity is increased by a number equal to half your Charisma modifier (rounded down).

entity.name: Spiritual Healer
entity.description:
Requirement: Charisma 7

When you successfully stabilize a Dying creature, you heal a number of HP equal to half your Healing Rate (rounded down).

effects.text: Spiritual Healer: When you successfully stabilize a Dying creature, you heal a number of HP equal to half your Healing Rate (rounded down).

entity.name: Backseat Driver
entity.description:
Requirement: Charisma 7

When you are a passenger in a Vehicle or Vertibird, the driver has advantage on any ability and skill checks.

effects.text: Backseat Driver: When you are a passenger in a Vehicle or Vertibird, the driver has advantage on any ability and skill checks.

entity.name: Hard Bargain
entity.description:
Requirement: Charisma 8

You gain an additional usage of the Discount ability before needing to take a Long Rest.

effects.text: Hard Bargain: You gain an additional usage of the Discount ability before needing to take a Long Rest.

entity.name: Wasteland Whisperer
entity.description:
Requirement: Charisma 8, Animal Friend

Can be taken 2 times.

On the first rank of this perk, you gain the ability to Pacify certain animals. You can attempt to pacify a creature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier. When attempting to Pacify an animal, roll a Charisma check to beat a DC determined by the animal you’re targeting, based on the table below. If you are in combat with that creature, you have disadvantage. Once a creature is Pacified, it will no longer be hostile to you but may be hostile to others around it. A creature will remain Pacified for a number of hours equal to your Charisma modifier. If you attack a Pacified creature, it is no longer Pacified.

On the second rank of this perk, you now have the capability to Tame certain animals. You can only attempt to Tame a creature once. When attempting to Tame an animal, you make the same Charisma check as before, however the DC is equal to the next tier above that creature type. If this creature has been Pacified, you have advantage. You cannot tame a Tier 5 creature. If you are in combat with that creature, you have disadvantage and you cannot attempt to tame it if you’ve already attacked it. Once a creature is tamed, it is friendly to you and your allies and will follow your commands during combat. You have 5 total “slots” for tamed creatures, with each creature taking a number of slots equal to its Tier. *(For example, a Deathclaw takes 4 slots.)

effects.text: Wasteland Whisperer: On the first rank of this perk, you gain the ability to Pacify certain animals. You can attempt to pacify a creature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier. When attempting to Pacify an animal, roll a Charisma check to beat a DC determined by the animal you’re targeting, based on the table below. If you are in combat with that creature, you have disadvantage. Once a creature is Pacified, it will no longer be hostile to you but may be hostile to others around it. A creature will remain Pacified for a number of hours equal to your Charisma modifier. If you attack a Pacified creature, it is no longer Pacified.

entity.name: Blood Sacrifice!
entity.description:
Requirement: Charisma 10

Whenever you are Dying, all other player characters gain +2 DT and +1 AC and heal 10 SP at the start of their turns. These effects cease once you stop Dying.

effects.text: Blood Sacrifice!: Whenever you are Dying, all other player characters gain +2 DT and +1 AC and heal 10 SP at the start of their turns. These effects cease once you stop Dying.

entity.name: Running On Empty
entity.description:
Requirement: Intelligence 5

When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird in combat and its Fuel Level reaches 0, the vehicle can continue moving for an additional turn before coming to a stop or landing. When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird during travel and its Fuel Level reaches 0, you can travel an additional hour before needing to refuel.

effects.text: Running On Empty: When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird in combat and its Fuel Level reaches 0, the vehicle can continue moving for an additional turn before coming to a stop or landing. When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird during travel and its Fuel Level reaches 0, you can travel an additional hour before needing to refuel.

entity.name: Grease Monkey
entity.description:
Requirement: Intelligence 7

When fixing a malfunction in a Vehicle or Vertibird, the Repair DC is decreased by 5. Additionally, all Crafting skill checks to repair a Vehicle or Vertibird have advantage and you use half as many materials (rounded down).

effects.text: Grease Monkey: When fixing a malfunction in a Vehicle or Vertibird, the Repair DC is decreased by 5. Additionally, all Crafting skill checks to repair a Vehicle or Vertibird have advantage and you use half as many materials (rounded down).

entity.name: Power User
entity.description:
Requirement: Intelligence 8

Can be taken 3 times.

For each rank of this perk, the Operation AP for all Power Armor is increased by 50.

effects.text: Power User: For each rank of this perk, the Operation AP for all Power Armor is increased by 50.

entity.name: Scrapper
entity.description:
Requirement: Intelligence 8

When breaking down weapons and armor for crafting materials, you gain advantage on the Crafting skill check and the DC decreases by 2.

effects.text: Scrapper: When breaking down weapons and armor for crafting materials, you gain advantage on the Crafting skill check and the DC decreases by 2.

entity.name: Gearhead
entity.description:
Requirement: Intelligence 8

Can be taken 3 times.

You gain an additional upgrade slot for any Vehicles or Vertibirds.

Each rank of this perk grants an additional upgrade slot.

effects.text: Gearhead: You gain an additional upgrade slot for any Vehicles or Vertibirds.

entity.name: Electric Absorption
entity.description:
Requirement: Intelligence 9

When you are wearing Power Armor and take electricity damage, the damage is halved and your Power Armor’s Operational AP increases by a number equal to half the damage (rounded down), to a maximum of 10. This cannot exceed the maximum Operational AP.

effects.text: Electric Absorption: When you are wearing Power Armor and take electricity damage, the damage is halved and your Power Armor’s Operational AP increases by a number equal to half the damage (rounded down), to a maximum of 10. This cannot exceed the maximum Operational AP.

entity.name: Artisan
entity.description:
Requirement: Intelligence 10

When you fully repair armor or weapons, you can optionally choose to repair an extra level of Decay, using the same amount of materials needed to repair one level. This sets your armor or weapon to -1 levels of Decay instead of 0. *(You cannot repair armor or weapons from 0 levels of Decay.)

When armor has -1 levels of Decay, it has +1 to its AC and DT. When a weapon has -1 levels of Decay, it has +1 to its attack roll. Once your armor or weapon takes a level of Decay after using this ability, the benefit is removed and the armor or weapon returns to 0 levels of Decay.

effects.text: Artisan: When you fully repair armor or weapons, you can optionally choose to repair an extra level of Decay, using the same amount of materials needed to repair one level. This sets your armor or weapon to -1 levels of Decay instead of 0. *(You cannot repair armor or weapons from 0 levels of Decay.)

entity.name: Power Armor Reboot
entity.description:
Requirement: Intelligence 10

When you are wearing Power Armor and fall to 0 HP, you can expend 100 Operational AP to instantly recover to half your max HP (rounded down).

effects.text: Power Armor Reboot: When you are wearing Power Armor and fall to 0 HP, you can expend 100 Operational AP to instantly recover to half your max HP (rounded down).

entity.name: Secret Agent
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 5

When you use Stealth Boys, the effect lasts an additional 30 seconds (5 rounds), increasing the total duration to 1 minute 30 seconds (15 rounds). Additionally, any Stealth Boys you use have two charges instead of one.

effects.text: Secret Agent: When you use Stealth Boys, the effect lasts an additional 30 seconds (5 rounds), increasing the total duration to 1 minute 30 seconds (15 rounds). Additionally, any Stealth Boys you use have two charges instead of one.

entity.name: Harrier
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 5

If you damage a creature’s SP or HP with 3 attacks from an Archery Weapon in a single turn, the creature loses 4 AP on their next turn.

effects.text: Harrier: If you damage a creature’s SP or HP with 3 attacks from an Archery Weapon in a single turn, the creature loses 4 AP on their next turn.

entity.name: Shifting Gears
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 5

When you are driving a Vehicle, changing the vehicle’s direction while moving only costs 1 AP.

effects.text: Shifting Gears: When you are driving a Vehicle, changing the vehicle’s direction while moving only costs 1 AP.

entity.name: Born Survivor
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 7

Whenever you take damage that reduces you to below 25% HP, you can choose to automatically use a Medicine or Chem that you have for no AP cost. This can only be done once per round.

effects.text: Born Survivor: Whenever you take damage that reduces you to below 25% HP, you can choose to automatically use a Medicine or Chem that you have for no AP cost. This can only be done once per round.

entity.name: Sweep The Leg
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 7

When you are within 5 ft. of a Medium or smaller creature, you can spend 5 AP to perform a special Unarmed Strike called a Takedown. If your attack hits, the target is knocked prone.

effects.text: Sweep The Leg: When you are within 5 ft. of a Medium or smaller creature, you can spend 5 AP to perform a special Unarmed Strike called a Takedown. If your attack hits, the target is knocked prone.

entity.name: Pedal to the Metal
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 7

When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird, its Speed modifier is doubled. In combat, you can choose whether or not to double the Speed modifier when moving.

effects.text: Pedal to the Metal: When you are driving a Vehicle or piloting a Vertibird, its Speed modifier is doubled. In combat, you can choose whether or not to double the Speed modifier when moving.

entity.name: Moving Target
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 8

For every 10 ft. you move on your turn by spending AP, your DT is increased by 1 until the start of your next turn.

effects.text: Moving Target: For every 10 ft. you move on your turn by spending AP, your DT is increased by 1 until the start of your next turn.

entity.name: Escape Artist
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 9

When you take the Hide action, you have +3 to your Sneak skill check. Additionally, if you succeed at hiding while in active combat, you go into the Hidden state rather than the Caution state, as long as the creature is not in direct line of sight to you. This means that enemies become fully unaware of your presence, and will not make checks to search for you.

effects.text: Escape Artist: When you take the Hide action, you have +3 to your Sneak skill check. Additionally, if you succeed at hiding while in active combat, you go into the Hidden state rather than the Caution state, as long as the creature is not in direct line of sight to you. This means that enemies become fully unaware of your presence, and will not make checks to search for you.

entity.name: Must’ve Been The Wind
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 9

If you are Hidden and kill an enemy with an Archery Weapon, you gain the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn.

effects.text: Must’ve Been The Wind: If you are Hidden and kill an enemy with an Archery Weapon, you gain the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn.

entity.name: Follow Through
entity.description:
Requirement: Agility 10

When you successfully make a Sneak Attack on another creature, for the next 2 rounds that creature will take an additional 1d8 damage from any attack you make.

effects.text: Follow Through: When you successfully make a Sneak Attack on another creature, for the next 2 rounds that creature will take an additional 1d8 damage from any attack you make.

entity.name: Plucky
entity.description:
Requirement: Luck 4

You find it easier to recover arrows and bolts from the bodies of your foes. The Luck ability check to recover arrows has its DC reduced by 2 (from 12 to 10). Additionally, whenever you hit an enemy with a Syringer syringe, the syringe is no longer destroyed and you can recover an Empty Syringe from their body once they die.

effects.text: Plucky: You find it easier to recover arrows and bolts from the bodies of your foes. The Luck ability check to recover arrows has its DC reduced by 2 (from 12 to 10). Additionally, whenever you hit an enemy with a Syringer syringe, the syringe is no longer destroyed and you can recover an Empty Syringe from their body once they die.

entity.name: Crash and Burn
entity.description:
Requirement: Luck 5

If a Vehicle/Vertibird you are driving/piloting or are a passenger in crashes, you and one other passenger of your choice miraculously take no impact damage. Additionally, if you would be knocked prone by a crash, you instead remain upright.

effects.text: Crash and Burn: If a Vehicle/Vertibird you are driving/piloting or are a passenger in crashes, you and one other passenger of your choice miraculously take no impact damage. Additionally, if you would be knocked prone by a crash, you instead remain upright.

entity.name: Down the Road
entity.description:
Requirement: Luck 7

Can be taken twice.

If a Vehicle/Vertibird you are driving/piloting or are a passenger in would suffer a malfunction, you can flip one of your Karma Caps to avoid the malfunction.

At 2nd rank of this perk, you can flip a Karma Cap to instantly repair a malfunction.

effects.text: Down the Road: Can be taken twice.

entity.name: Miss Fortune
entity.description:
Requirement: Luck 8

Only one party member can have this perk. Incompatible with the Mysterious Stranger perk.

Just when your enemies think they have the upper hand, Miss Fortune appears to turn their world upside down. When you take this perk, choose a number between 2 and 19. When an enemy targets you with an attack, if the base result without any modifiers matches your chosen number, the attack misses and Miss Fortune appears!

Roll a d20 (optionally, add your Luck ability modifier) and consult the table below for the effect:

effects.text: Miss Fortune: Only one party member can have this perk. Incompatible with the Mysterious Stranger perk.

entity.name: Lucky Break
entity.description:
Requirement: Luck 8

Whenever you damage a target’s HP, you can choose to expend 1 AP to make a DC 20 Luck ability check. On a success, your equipped weapon loses a level of Decay. You can only do this once per attack.

Additionally, whenever your armor’s DT blocks any damage, you can use your reaction to make a DC 20 Luck ability check. On a success, your armor loses a level of Decay. You can only do this once per hit you take.

effects.text: Lucky Break: Whenever you damage a target’s HP, you can choose to expend 1 AP to make a DC 20 Luck ability check. On a success, your equipped weapon loses a level of Decay. You can only do this once per attack.

entity.name: Kleptomaniac Punch
entity.description:
Requirement: Luck 8

When you deal damage to a target’s HP with an Unarmed Weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, as long as you have an open hand, make a DC 18 Luck ability check. On a success, you steal the weapon currently equipped by the target, if they have one. You automatically equip this weapon. If your attack critically hits and damages the target’s HP, you automatically succeed the check.

effects.text: Kleptomaniac Punch: When you deal damage to a target’s HP with an Unarmed Weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, as long as you have an open hand, make a DC 18 Luck ability check. On a success, you steal the weapon currently equipped by the target, if they have one. You automatically equip this weapon. If your attack critically hits and damages the target’s HP, you automatically succeed the check.

entity.name: Collateral Damage
entity.description:
Requirement: Luck 10

When you bring a creature to 0 HP with an attack, make a DC 20 Luck ability check. On a success, the enemy violently explodes, dealing 4d8 explosive damage to any creature within 5 ft. of the enemy of your choice. If this explosion brings another creature to 0 HP, you can make another Luck ability check to see if that creature explodes as well, however the DC is increased by +1. The DC resets once you run out of creatures or fail a check.

effects.text: Collateral Damage: When you bring a creature to 0 HP with an attack, make a DC 20 Luck ability check. On a success, the enemy violently explodes, dealing 4d8 explosive damage to any creature within 5 ft. of the enemy of your choice. If this explosion brings another creature to 0 HP, you can make another Luck ability check to see if that creature explodes as well, however the DC is increased by +1. The DC resets once you run out of creatures or fail a check.

fields.description: A Blinded creature can’t see and automatically fails any ability check that requires sight. Attack rolls against a Blinded creature have advantage. A Blinded can make blind attacks if they’re aware of a creature.
A Burning creature takes 1d10 fire damage at the start of their turns. They can spend 6 AP to put themselves out.
A Buzzed creature has disadvantage on all Perception and Intelligence ability and skill checks, as well as advantage on all Endurance and Strength ability and skill checks.
A Dazed creature’s maximum AP is decreased by 3 and they do not recycle any unused AP on their turns. Additionally, they no longer lose levels of Fatigue at the end of their turns.
A Deafened creature cannot hear and automatically fails any ability check that requires hearing.

entity.name: Diseased
entity.description: A Diseased creature is suffering a disease. When this creature damages a target's HP with a Melee or Unarmed attack, the target must make a Disease check.

fields.description: A Drunk creature has the effects of Buzzed. Additionally, your maximum AP is decreased by 2 and your maximum SP increases by a number equal to your level.

You fall prone and your total AP is reduced to 0. At the start of each of your turns, you gain 4 AP. You regain all unspent AP at the start of your turns, however you cannot have more than 6 AP. Moving 5 ft. costs 2 AP and you cannot move more than 10 ft. on your turn.
An Encumbered creature moves slowly (2 AP per 5 ft.). The creature’s travel pace is halved and you gain a level of Fatigue and Exhaustion for every hour you travel.

entity.name: Frenzied
entity.description: A Frenzied creature will become hostile to any creatures nearby, including neutral creatures or allies. It must attack the closest creature to it on its turn.

fields.description: A Frightened creature has disadvantage on any ability and skill check, including attack rolls, while the source of their fear is in their line of sight. Additionally, the creature cannot willingly move towards the source of their fear. At the end of every turn you are Frightened, you may make a DC 14 END ability check. If you succeed, you lose the Frightened condition.
A Grappled creature cannot spend AP to move. They can spend 5 AP to attempt to Escape a Grapple.
A Hammered creature has the effects of Buzzed and Drunk. Additionally, your maximum SP further increases by a number equal to your level, and your d20 rolls are reduced by 5.

A Heavily Encumbered creature moves very slowly (3 AP per 5 ft.). The creature’s travel pace is halved and for every hour you travel, your maximum SP is reduced by 2. Every day a Heavily Encumbered creature travels, their Carry Load decreases by 10.

Effects reset upon resting.

An Invisible creature is impossible to see and is considered Heavily Obscured. The creature’s location can be determined by noise it makes or any tracks it leaves. Any attack made against the creature will be a Blind Attack. Attack rolls made by the creature have advantage.

entity.name: Paralyzed
entity.description: A Paralyzed creature cannot make any actions or speak, but remains aware of the world around them. All its SP drops to 0.

fields.description: A Poisoned creature has disadvantage on all d20 rolls and takes 1d8 poison damage to their HP at the start of their turns. (Certain poisons may deal different amounts of damage.)

A Prone creature’s only movement option is to crawl, which costs 2 AP for every 5 ft. of movement. A creature can spend 5 AP to stand up and end this condition. The creature has disadvantage on attack rolls. Attacks against that creature have disadvantage unless the attacker is within 5 ft. of the creature, giving the attacker advantage.
A Restrained creature cannot move, and any damage it takes is dealt directly to its HP.
A creature in Shock has disadvantage on all d20 rolls and cannot regain any SP.
A Slowed creature starts their turn with a maximum of 6 AP.

An Unconscious creature cannot make any actions or speak and is unaware of the world around them. All its SP drops to 0. As long as you do not have 0 HP, at the start of your turns, you can choose to make a DC 14 END ability check to try and wake up. If you succeed, you wake up with the Dazed condition for 1 round. Every time you fail this check, the DC decreases by 1.
A Wasted creature has the effects of Buzzed, Drunk and Hammered. Additionally, you can remember nothing from the time you are Wasted and fall Unconscious after 1 hour.

entity.name: Anabolic Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: You have disadvantage on Strength and Endurance ability and skill checks.

entity.name: Anxiolytic Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: You have disadvantage on all Perception ability and skill checks.

entity.name: Anesthetic Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: When you take damage to your HP, the damage is increased by 2.

entity.name: Articulative Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: You have disadvantage on all Charisma ability and skill checks.

entity.name: Extrapolating Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: Your Passive Sense decreases by 5.

entity.name: Hallucinogenic Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: Your Karma Cap no longer flips back over if you critically fail or are critically hit by an attack.

entity.name: Sedative Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: Any attack you make is decreased by 2.

entity.name: Stimulant Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: You have disadvantage on all Agility ability and skill checks.

entity.name: Neuro-Stimulant Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: You have disadvantage on all Intelligence ability and skill checks.

entity.name: Psychosis Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: Your AC decreases by 2.

entity.name: Painkiller Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: Your maximum HP is reduced by a number equal to your level.

entity.name: X-Cell Addiction
entity.description: Withdrawal: All SPECIAL stats are decreased by 1.

fields.description: A weapon that has these properties requires certain types of ammo or fuel to operate at full capacity. The required ammo/fuel is listed next to the Ammo property. As long as the weapon has ammo/fuel, you deal the listed damage normally. If the weapon runs out of ammo/fuel, you deal the damage listed next to the Depleted property. You can spend 6 AP to reload the weapon with the required ammo/fuel.
A weapon that has this property gains a level of Decay when you roll a 3 or lower on an attack roll.

When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a weapon that has this property, the target becomes Grappled and any Strength/Agility checks to escape the grapple have disadvantage. If the target is one size larger than you, it can only be grappled if your Strength score is 10. Targets two or more sizes larger than you cannot be grappled in this way.

When you attack with a weapon that has this property, you can spend an additional 3 AP to also target two additional areas with the attack roll, as long as the two additional areas are within 5 ft. of the original target. Each creature is individually targeted by the same attack roll, and will take damage if the attack beats their AC. If a single creature occupies two or all of the areas, they take damage from each attack roll. (If the weapon says “Always Cleaves”, you do not need to spend the additional 3 AP to make this special attack.)

When you deal damage to a target’s HP from a targeted attack with a weapon that has this property, you roll twice for the Conditions and apply both Conditions. If you roll the same Condition twice, the effects stack.
If you block while holding a weapon that has this property, your DT increases by 2.
Targeted Attacks to the arms or legs do not cost additional AP with this weapon. Additionally, if you bring a creature to 0 HP with this weapon, you may choose to dismember their head or a limb.
A weapon that has this property does not gain levels of Decay when you throw it or roll a 1 on the attack roll.
When a weapon that has this property gains a level of Decay, it immediately gains 10 levels of Decay and breaks, ceasing function.
When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a weapon that has this property, they gain 1 level of Bleeding, or 1 level of Short Circuit if they are a Robot/Gen-2 Synth.
When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a critical hit with a weapon that has this property, they gain 2 levels of Bleeding, or 2 levels of Short Circuit if they are a Robot/Gen-2 Synth.
The reach of a weapon that has this property is increased by 5 ft..

A weapon with this property can be used to revitalize dying creatures. With 6 AP, you can expend a charge to stabilize a Dying creature within 5 ft. of you. The Dying creature gains HP equal to their half their Healing Rate and loses the Dying condition.
A weapon that has this property does not gain levels of Decay if you throw it, and it ignores the negative effects of the first 2 levels of Decay.

When you attack with a weapon that has this property, you can throw the weapon a number of ft. equal to your Strength score multiplied by the values listed after Thrown. The first number is the short range you can throw the weapon, the second number is the long range you can throw the weapon. If the target is past the short range of the weapon, you have disadvantage on the attack roll.

If you hold a weapon that has this property with one hand and attack with it, you must spend an additional 2 AP. Otherwise, you have disadvantage on the attack roll. If your Strength score is greater than the weapon’s Strength requirement by at least 3, you ignore this property.
When you attack with an Unarmed Weapon, you add your Unarmed skill modifier to the attack roll instead of the Melee Weapons skill modifier.
Whenever you roll a 1 on the damage dice with a weapon that has this property, it is a 2 instead.
When you deal damage with a weapon that has this property, you do not add your ability score modifier to the damage roll.
When you make a targeted attack with a weapon that has this property, you may choose the limb condition instead of rolling for it.

When you deal damage to a creature with a weapon that has this property, the energy leaps to a nearby creature within 20 ft. of the previously damaged creature and makes another attack with the same attack roll, dealing the same damage if it beats the creature’s AC. This continues as long as there is a new target within 20 ft. of the previous one or until the attack misses.

When you attack with a weapon that has this property, you do not make an attack roll. Instead, you use the required ammo and any creatures or objects in range take the weapon’s damage when the attack hits. You do not add your Agility modifier to this damage. You cannot make a Targeted Attack with an Area of Effect weapon.

When you spend AP to make an attack with a weapon that has this property, you can make a number of additional attacks without spending extra AP. The number of additional attacks you can make is listed in the Special Properties of the weapon. The target(s) of these attacks must be within 10 ft. of the original target, and you do not add your Agility/Perception modifier to any additional damage rolls. When you make a Targeted Attack with a weapon that has this property, only the first attack will act as a targeted attack, and any additional attacks will be normal attacks.

A weapon that has this property has the ability to switch between Automatic and Single Shot. You can spend 1 AP to switch between the two modes. When attacking on Single Shot mode, the weapon functions normally and has the Special Properties listed after Single Shot. When attacking on Automatic mode, the weapon functions as an Automatic weapon (see Automatic property above) and has the Special Properties listed after Automatic.
A weapon that has this property gains a level of Decay when you roll a 3 or lower on an attack roll.

When you spend AP to attack with a weapon that has this property, you can spend 3 additional AP to add 1 additional damage dice to the damage roll. You can do this twice for an attack, so +6 AP for +2 damage dice. Whenever you charge a weapon, you add your relevant Ability modifier to the damage twice instead of once.

When you deal damage to a creature’s HP with a weapon that has this property, their armor gains a level of Decay. If they have natural armor, their AC and DT are decreased by 1 until their HP is fully healed. This has no effect on Power Armor.

When you deal damage to a creature’s HP from a targeted attack with a weapon that has this property, you roll twice for the Conditions and apply both Conditions. If you roll the same Condition twice, the effects stack. If the weapon also has the Accurate property, you can only choose one Condition.
If you block while holding a weapon that has this property, your DT increases by 2.
Whenever you roll a 1 on the damage dice with a weapon that has this property, it is a 2 instead.
A weapon that has this property does not gain levels of Decay when you roll critically fail on the attack roll.
A weapon with this property deals electricity damage. Additionally, it deals double damage against creatures in Power Armor.

When you attack with an Energy Weapon, you add your Energy Weapons skill modifier to the attack roll instead of your Guns skill modifier. When you deal damage with an Energy Weapon, you add your Perception modifier instead of your Agility modifier. If you bring an enemy to 0 HP with a critical hit from a weapon with this property, they are reduced to an ash pile (for laser, fire, and electricity damage) or a pile of goo (for plasma damage). Their bodies can still be looted.

When you deal damage to a target with a weapon that has this property, they gain the Slowed condition until the end of their next turn. If an attack with this weapon damages a target’s HP, they gain a level of Hypothermia.

When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a weapon that has this property, they gain the Burning condition. If an attack with this weapon misses, the projectile may land nearby and start a fire (up to Overseer’s discretion). Any flammable objects hit by a weapon that has this property will immediately burst into flames.
If you hold a weapon that has this property with one hand, both the short and long range are halved.
When you spend AP to reload a weapon that has this property, you must spend 1 AP to load 1 round into the weapon.

When you deal damage to a creature within 5 ft. of you with a weapon that has this property, you deal the maximum damage for that weapon. Additionally, you deal any additional effects of a Critical Hit (but not the damage bonus/modifier). (For example, a weapon that deals 2d12 damage will deal 24 damage.)
When you spend AP to reload a weapon that has this property, the action only costs 4 AP instead of 6 AP.
When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a weapon that has this property, the target must succeed a Radiation Check or take 1 level of Radiation.

If you spend AP to attack with a weapon that has this property directly after spending AP to make an attack on the same turn, you can make an additional attack without spending any AP. This additional attack cannot be a Targeted Attack. (If you make 2 attacks with a Semi-Automatic weapon on the same turn, you can make a 3rd attack for free.)

When you attack with a weapon that has this property, the target is not hit until the start of your next turn. If your target is no longer in range once your turn arrives, you miss and deal no damage.

When you spend AP to reload a weapon that has this property, it costs 10 AP instead of 6 AP. If you are within 5 ft. of another creature, that creature can spend 5 AP on their turn to help you reload the weapon, lowering your cost to 5 AP. If your maximum AP is 9 or less, you must spend the additional AP on your next turn in order to reload the weapon.

When you attack a target past the short range of a weapon that has this property, you also target additional creatures or objects within 5 ft. of the target with the same attack roll. The number of additional targets is equal to the weapon’s damage die number (ie. a weapon that deals 3d8 damage can hit 3 additional targets). If hit, the additional targets take damage equal to the weapon’s damage with its damage die number reduced by 1 (ie. 3d8 damage becomes 2d8 for additional targets). If there is only one damage die, the damage die instead decreases a rank (to a minimum of 1d4). This damage roll does not have any modifiers applied. Additional targets take no extra critical hit damage.
A weapon that has this property ignores the negative effects of the first 2 levels of Decay.

If you hold a weapon that has this property with one hand and attack with it, you must spend an additional 2 AP. Otherwise, you have disadvantage on the attack roll and after attacking, you fall prone. If your Strength ability score is greater than the weapon’s Strength requirement by at least 3, you ignore this property.
A weapon that has this property gains a level of Decay every 5 times you reload it instead of 10.
If you hold a weapon that has this property with one hand and attack, you have disadvantage on the attack roll, unless your Perception is a 10.
Each creature in the area of effect listed next to the *Blinding* property gains the Blinded condition for a number of rounds equal to 4 - their Endurance modifier, to a minimum of 1.
Each creature in the area of effect listed next to the *Deafening* property gains the Deafened condition for a number of rounds equal to 4 - their Endurance modifier, to a minimum of 1.
Whenever you roll a 1 on the damage dice with an explosive that has this property, it is a 2 instead.

An explosive with this property doesn’t detonate after any amount of time has passed; instead it will only detonate once you spend 3 AP on your turn to detonate it, as long as you are within the range listed next to the *Detonator* property.

Whenever an explosive that has this property damages the HP of a target in the first range (*taking full damage*), they gain 2 random leg conditions, or 1 random arm condition if they are prone when the explosive detonates. If the explosive deals enough damage to bring the target to 0 HP, the limb is severed.
An explosive that has this property deals Electricity damage.
When a target takes damage from an explosive that has this property, they gain the Slowed condition until the end of their next turn.
When a target takes damage from an explosive that has this property, they gain the Burning condition.
When a target takes damage to their HP from an explosive that has this property, they gain a level of Bleeding, or a level of Short Circuit if they are a Robot/Gen-2 Synth.

An explosive that has this property doesn’t detonate after any amount of time has passed; instead it will only detonate once a creature enters a 10 ft. radius proximity area around the explosive for the first time on a turn. The explosive detonates at the end of that creature’s turn.
An explosive that has this property always detonates at the end of your turn regardless of your Explosives roll.
An explosive that has this property will detonate after an amount of time listed next to the *Slow* property has passed.

When an explosive that has this property detonates, it creates a cloud of smoke in the area of effect listed next to the *Smoke* property. The smoke spreads around corners, the area of effect is considered Heavily Obscured, and any creatures within the area of effect gain the Blinded condition. The smoke lasts for 1 minute.

If you consume a drink with the Alcoholic or High-Proof property that also has this property, you must make a DC 5 Endurance ability check. If you fail, you become addicted to alcoholic drinks. When addicted, you always have 2 levels of Exhaustion unless you are Drunk. You lose the addiction if you spend a number of weeks equal to 6 - your Endurance modifier without drinking any alcohol.

When you consume a drink that has this property and your Endurance ability score is 5 or higher, you gain the Buzzed condition for 1d4 hours. If your Endurance ability score is 4 or lower, you instead gain the Drunk condition for 1d4 hours. If you already have the Buzzed condition and consume another Alcoholic or High-Proof drink, you gain the Drunk condition for 1d4 hours. If you already have the Drunk condition and consume another 2 Alcoholic or High-Proof drinks, you gain the Hammered condition for 1d4 hours. If you are already Hammered and consume another 2 Alcoholic or High-Proof drinks, you gain the Wasted condition for 1d4 hours.

If you consume a food or drink that has this property, you no longer suffer the negative effects of the first 3 levels of Exhaustion for the next 6 hours. If you have no levels of Exhaustion, you can add +1 to any d20 roll for the next 6 hours. If you drink another Caffeinated drink while already under the effects of one, you gain 1 AP at the start of your turns for the next 6 hours. However, once those 6 hours are up, you gain 1 level of Exhaustion for every extra Caffeinated drink you consume.

When you consume a drink that has this property and your Endurance ability score is 5 or higher, you gain the Drunk condition for 1d4 hours. If your Endurance ability score is 4 or lower, you instead gain the Hammered condition for 1d4 hours. If you already have the Drunk condition and consume another Alcoholic or High-Proof drink, you gain the Hammered condition for 1d4 hours. If you already have the Hammered condition and consume another 2 Alcoholic or High-Proof drinks, you gain the Wasted condition for 1d4 hours.
When you consume a drink that has this property, you remove 3 levels of Dehydration instead of 1. Additionally, you remove a level of Overheating.

Some foods aren’t entirely the safest to eat, but beggars can’t be choosers in the wasteland. When you consume a food that has this property, you gain 1 Rads. If you gain 10 Rads, you gain 1 level of Radiation. You can take Rad-Away to remove all Rads.
When you consume food that has this property, you remove 2 levels of Hunger instead of 1.
When you consume food that has this property, you heal a number of SP equal to half your level.
When you consume food that has this property, you heal a number of SP equal to your level.
When you consume food that has this property, you heal a number of SP equal to double your level.
When you consume food that has this property, you heal a number of SP equal to triple your level.
When you consume food that has this property, your Radiation DC decreases by 2 for the next 6 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, you gain 1 AP at the start of your turns for the next 4 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, you gain 2 AP at the start of your turns for the next 4 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, you heal a number of HP equal to your Healing Rate.
When you consume food that has this property, you remove 1 level of Dehydration.
Consumed with 3 AP instead of 4. When you consume food that has this property, you only remove half a level of Hunger.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, your DT is increased by 3 against Fire and Laser damage for the next 6 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, your Carry Load increases by 50 for the next 6 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, your DT increases by 1 for the next 6 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property and your Endurance is 5 or lower, you gain the Poisoned condition for 4 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, you are cured of one addiction.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, your damage from attacks increases by 2 for the next 4 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, you have advantage on all Luck ability checks for the next 6 hours.
When you consume a food or drink that has this property, you recycle all your unspent AP at the beginning of your turns instead of half for the next 1 hour.
If you use a chem with this property, you have advantage on all Strength and Endurance ability and skill checks. Additionally, you gain temporary HP equal to your level.
If you use a chem with this property, your DT increases by 6.
If you use a chem with this property, you have advantage on Combat Sequence rolls and any checks to resist becoming Frightened.
If you use a chem with this property, you have advantage on all Intelligence and Perception ability and skill checks, however you have disadvantage on all Charisma ability and skill checks.
If you use a chem with this property, you have advantage on all Luck ability checks and you may flip one of your Karma Caps back up.

If you use a chem with this property, you gain 4 AP at the start of your turn (to a maximum of 20). You no longer suffer the negative effects of the first 8 levels of Exhaustion. If you have no levels of Exhaustion, add +2 to every d20 roll. Additionally, you are immune to gaining levels of Fatigue. However, your Addiction DC is 10 instead of 6.
If you use a chem with this property, you regain SP equal to half your level (rounded up).
If you use a chem with this property, your DT increases by 3.

If you use a chem with this property, when you hit with an attack, the damage is increased by 5. However, you must always attack the nearest hostile creature on your turn. If there are no hostile creatures nearby, you must make an Endurance ability check with a DC of 15. If you fail, you must attack the nearest neutral or friendly creature.
If you use a chem with this property, you gain 1 AP at the start of your turn (to a maximum of 16) and have advantage on all Intelligence and Perception ability and skill checks.
If you use a chem with this property, your Passive Sense increases by 5 and your Critical Hits deal an extra 10 damage.

If you use a chem with this property, you gain 1 AP at the start of your turn (to a maximum of 16). You no longer suffer the negative effects of the first 3 levels of Exhaustion. If you have no levels of Exhaustion, add +1 to every d20 roll.

If you use a chem with this property, you gain 2 AP at the start of your turn (to a maximum of 20). You no longer suffer the negative effects of the first 5 levels of Exhaustion. If you have no levels of Exhaustion, add +2 to every d20 roll. Additionally, you are immune to gaining levels of Fatigue. However, your Addiction DC is 8 instead of 6.

entity.name: Armor Piercing
entity.description: When you deal damage to a creature’s HP with a weapon that has this property, it ignores up to 8 DT. When you deal damage to the Defense Points of Power Armor, it deals an additional 8 damage.

entity.name: Fragile
entity.description: When a weapon that has this property gains a level of Decay, it immediately gains 10 levels of Decay and breaks, ceasing function.

entity.name: Low Penetration
entity.description: When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a weapon that has this property, the target’s DT is effectively doubled.

entity.name: Mangle
entity.description: When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a weapon that has this property, they gain a level of Bleeding, or a level of Short Circuit if they are a Robot/Gen-2 Synth.

entity.name: Recharging
entity.description: A weapon that has this property generates 1 ammo unit at the start of the wielder’s turn, with a limit of the weapon’s ammo capacity. Ammo will only generate when the weapon is equipped.

entity.name: Silent
entity.description: A weapon that has this property comes with a built-in Silencer. Any attack made with this weapon while hidden will not reveal your position.

entity.name: Weak
entity.description: When you deal damage with a weapon that has this property, you do not add your ability score modifier to the damage roll.

entity.name: Armor Piercing
entity.description: When you deal damage to a creature’s HP with a weapon that has this property, it ignores up to 5 DT. When you deal damage to the Defense Points of Power Armor, it deals an additional 5 damage.

entity.name: Automatic
entity.description: When you spend AP to make an attack with a weapon that has this property, you can make a number of additional attacks without spending extra AP. The number of additional attacks you can make is listed in the Special Properties of the weapon. The target(s) of these attacks must be within 5 ft. of you, and you do not add your Strength ability modifier to any additional damage rolls. When you make a Targeted Attack with a weapon that has this property, only the first attack will act as a targeted attack. Any additional attacks will be normal attacks.

entity.name: Fatiguing
entity.description: When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a weapon that has this property, they gain a level of Fatigue.

entity.name: Loud
entity.description: When you have this weapon equipped, you automatically fail any Sneak check to go unnoticed and any enemy within 10 ft. of you becomes aware of your position. If the weapon is Depleted, this property no longer has any effect.

entity.name: Improvised
entity.description: A weapon that has this property counts as an Improvised Weapon.

entity.name: Fatiguing
entity.description: When a target takes damage from an explosive that has this property, they gain 2 levels of Fatigue.

entity.name: Quick
entity.description: A proximity explosive that has this property will detonate immediately upon being triggered.

entity.name: Heavy Reload
entity.description: A weapon with this property is reloaded with 5 AP.

entity.name: Silent
entity.description: A weapon that has this property is naturally silent. Any attack made with this weapon while Hidden will not reveal your position.

entity.name: Charge
entity.description: When you spend AP to attack with a weapon that has this property, you can spend 3 additional AP to add 1 additional damage dice to the damage roll. You can do this twice for an attack, so +6 AP for +2 damage dice. Whenever you charge an archery weapon, you add your Endurance ability modifier to the damage twice instead of once.

entity.name: Durable
entity.description: A weapon that has this property does not gain levels of Decay when you roll a 1 on the attack roll.

entity.name: Semi-Automatic
entity.description: If you spend AP to attack with a weapon that has this property directly after spending AP to make an attack on the same turn, you can make an additional attack without spending any AP. (If you make 2 attacks with a Semi-Automatic weapon on the same turn, you can make a 3rd attack for free.)

entity.name: Drawstring
entity.description: This weapon must be operated with two hands in order to hold the weapon and pull back the draw string. It cannot be shot with one hand.

entity.name: Appetite Suppressant
entity.description: When you consume food that has this property, you ignore the negative effects of the first 2 levels of Hunger for the next 1 hour.

entity.name: Dehydrating
entity.description: When you consume a food or drink that has this property, you gain a level of Dehydration.

entity.name: Empty
entity.description: When you consume a food that has this property, you regain no levels of Hunger. Foods with this property are often used as components rather than proper food.

entity.name: Cannibalistic

fields.description:
Cloth armor doesn’t provide much protection. However it lends its simplicity to being light and having the most amount of upgrade slots. Most vault suits are considered cloth armor.

Load: 5 (not worn), 2 (worn).

Armor Properties

All types of armor have general properties.

Armor Class (AC). A representation of how tough your armor is. Armor with a higher AC is made of stronger materials that completely protect you. While you wear armor, your AC is equal to the number listed in the AC column of the Armor Types table. If an attack roll’s total is equal to or greater than your AC, you take damage. Your AC starts at 10 when wearing no armor.

Damage Threshold (DT). The measurement of how much the armor protects you. Armor with a higher DT covers more of your body, protecting you from all attacks. Whenever you take damage to your HP, the damage is reduced by a number equal to your DT. The DT is listed in the DT column of the Armor Types table. Your DT can never be lower than 0.

Carry Load & Strength Requirement. A representation of how heavy the armor is and how much space it takes up. If you are wearing the armor, its load is halved (rounded down). If you are wearing armor that you do not meet the Strength requirement for, you have the Slowed condition.

Upgrade Slots. Armor can be customized with upgrades. The number of upgrades it can have is listed in the Slots column. Ranks in an upgrade do not count against the armor’s slot total.

Decay. Whenever you get critically hit or fall to 0 HP, your armor gains a level of Decay. The armor’s AC and DT are decreased by a number equal to half its levels of Decay, rounded down. AC has a minimum of 10, DT has a minimum of 0.

A jacket, fittings around the arms, knee pads, and boots all fall under leather armor. Leather isn’t very tough but can fit easily around one’s body.

Load: 15 (not worn), 7 (worn).

In the wasteland, you take what you can get. Metal armor is a combination of various pieces that have been welded or fitted around the body. Granting toughness but allowing less coverage.

Load: 20 (not worn), 10 (worn).

A combination of vestments. Layers of leather, cloth, tarp, metal, anything lying around to act as armor is considered multilayered. This armor provides maximum coverage but sacrifices toughness.

Load: 40 (not worn), 20 (worn).

Bulletproof vests, kevlar, or military grade jackets. Ballistic weave is a pre-war synthetic fiber whose reproduction has been lost with the war. Extremely rare but provides the best of all armor aspects; coverage, toughness, and weight.

Load: 10 (not worn), 5 (worn).

Fitted plates of metal that cover the body like a knight provide a modern solution in the apocalypse for dealing with threats. Steel maximizes coverage and toughness, so long as you have the strength.

Load: 50 (not worn), 25 (worn).

entity.name: Raider
entity.description:
Raider: AC 13, DP 8, 6 upgrade slots, repair DC 14, 150 AP of operation. Special properties: Clunky.

All Power Armor comes with a standard set of features.

Operation. It costs 6 AP to enter or exit Power Armor.

Defense Points (DP). When you enter Power Armor, you gain a new set of points called Defense Points. Defense Points operate similarly to SP - whenever you take damage to your SP or HP, it is dealt to your DP instead. DP cannot be bypassed unless explicitly stated by an ability. DP is not modified by any ability scores, and is instead a flat amount set by each type of Power Armor listed in the DP column of the Power Armor Types table.

When your DP reaches 0, the Power Armor gains a level of Decay and its DP resets. Once the Power Armor reaches 10 levels of Decay, it no longer has any DP and does not provide any additional DT, however its AC remains the same.

Repair. Unlike other weapons and armor, levels of Decay do not apply any negative effects to the armor or user and Power Armor does not cease to function when it reaches 10 levels of Decay.

To repair any levels of Decay from Power Armor, you must spend at least 15 minutes per level of Decay you attempt to repair, have the materials (5 steel, 3 circuitry, 3 aluminum, and 3 adhesive), and roll a successful Crafting check against the DC listed in the Repair column of the Power Armor Types table.

Fusion Core. Power Armor requires a special type of condensed nuclear power called a Fusion Core to operate. You can spend 5 AP on your turn to replace the Fusion Core on a set of Power Armor. It slots into its back and provides Operation AP. Each Power Armor has its own Operation AP, listed in the Operation AP column of the Power Armor Types table.

This Operation AP works as a resource pool that every action that uses AP draws from. When you make an action that uses AP, the amount of AP used is subtracted from the Operation AP as well as your max AP on that turn. When outside of combat, assume that 50 Operation AP is spent for every 1 hour of operation.

Once the Operation AP reaches 0, the Power Armor pulls power from its emergency reserves granting it 15 AP for operation. After this 15 AP is spent, the power armor uses its last amount of power to open its back to allow its user to exit the armor. Then, it ceases function. If necessary, you can choose to override this function to keep yourself in the power armor. However, while in this state you are Grappled and Restrained, and you cannot escape unless you succeed a DC 25 Strength ability check. Escaping in this way causes the Power Armor to gain 10 levels of Decay.

Overheating. If you spend more than 15 AP on one turn while wearing Power Armor, it becomes Overheated until the beginning of your next turn. When Power Armor becomes Overheated, the armor loses 100 Operation AP.

If this drains the Operation AP to 0, the operator is ejected from the Power Armor and the Fusion Core will explode at the end of their next turn. This explosion has a radius of 20/50 ft. and deals 20d10 explosive damage. The Power Armor is destroyed and, if the operator is still inside, they are instantly incinerated and die. The explosion area becomes a Level 5 Irradiated Zone.

Fusion Core Targeting. Power Armor has a significant weakness: its Fusion Core is exposed to allow itself to cool. Any creature who can see the back of a creature wearing Power Armor can make a Targeted Attack at the Fusion Core. This Targeted Attack costs +5 AP, deals no damage to the armor or its operator, and applies no conditions. Every time the Fusion Core takes 30 damage, it becomes Overheated until the operator’s next turn.

Upgrade Slots. Power Armor can be customized with upgrades. The number of upgrades it can have is listed in the Slots column of the Power Armor Types table. Ranks in an upgrade do not count against the power armor’s slot total.

Carry Load & Strength Requirement. All Power Armor has a Carry Load of 100. If you are wearing the Power Armor, its Carry Load is 0. Power Armor has no Strength Requirement, as its interior chassis supports its user entirely. Even if you are missing limbs, you can still use Power Armor.

Hydraulic Machine. Your Strength ability score is considered a 12 (+7) and your size is Large while wearing Power Armor. Additionally, Unarmed Strikes now use d8s instead of d6s for the damage die.

Longer Strides. If you Sprint in Power Armor, you can move an additional 20 ft..

Calibrated Impact Servos. If you would be knocked Prone, you can instead spend 5 DP to stay standing up, and if you are subjected to an effect that would push you back or pull you, you move half the distance you normally would. Additionally, you are resistant to impact damage.

Automatic Injector. While wearing Power Armor, you can use any chem or Stimpak with only 1 AP.

Lead Plated Exoskeleton. You do not suffer any limb conditions from Targeted Attacks and your limbs cannot be severed. Additionally, if your Power Armor has less than 6 levels of Decay, you are immune to Radiation. If your Power Armor has 6 to 9 levels of Decay, you have advantage on Radiation checks. If your Power Armor has 10 levels of Decay, it offers no protection against Radiation.

Oxygen Tank. You can breathe underwater, however you cannot swim and you sink at a rate of 100 ft. each round.

Atmospheric Seal. As long as your helmet is on, you are immune to any air-based hazards, such as toxic air, smoke, or airborne disease. If your Power Armor has more than 8 levels of Decay, you lose the benefit of this property.

Power Armor Special Properties

Heat Resistant. When wearing the Power Armor, you take twice as long to gain levels of Overheating and are resistant to fire damage.

Cold Resistant. When wearing the Power Armor, you take twice as long to gain levels of Hypothermia and are resistant to cold damage.

Industrial. While wearing the Power Armor, your Strength ability score is considered a 15 instead of a 12. Additionally, Carry Load increases by 50.

Recycling. While wearing this Power Armor, whenever you consume 8 oz of a liquid, it is converted into 4 oz of Purified Water. (2 drinks recycles into 1 Purified Water).

Intimidating. While wearing this Power Armor, you have disadvantage on all Charisma ability and skill checks except for Intimidation skill checks, which you have advantage on.

Clunky. While wearing this Power Armor, you have disadvantage on any non-combat Agility ability or skill checks. Attack rolls are unaffected.

Prototype. Whenever this Power Armor gains a level of Decay, it gains twice as many.

Prototype. Whenever this Power Armor gains a level of Decay, it gains twice as many.

Every time the Fusion Core takes 30 damage, it becomes Overheated until the operator’s next turn.

Upgrade Slots. Power Armor can be customized with upgrades. The number of upgrades it can have is listed in the Slots column of the Power Armor Types table. Ranks in an upgrade do not count against the power armor’s slot total.

Carry Load & Strength Requirement. All Power Armor has a Carry Load of 100. If you are wearing the Power Armor, its Carry Load is 0. Power Armor has no Strength Requirement, as its interior chassis supports its user entirely. Even if you are missing limbs, you can still use Power Armor.

Hydraulic Machine. Your Strength ability score is considered a 12 (+7) and your size is Large while wearing Power Armor. Additionally, Unarmed Strikes now use d8s instead of d6s for the damage die.

Longer Strides. If you Sprint in Power Armor, you can move an additional 20 ft..

Calibrated Impact Servos. If you would be knocked Prone, you can instead spend 5 DP to stay standing up, and if you are subjected to an effect that would push you back or pull you, you move half the distance you normally would. Additionally, you are resistant to impact damage.

Automatic Injector. While wearing Power Armor, you can use any chem or Stimpak with only 1 AP.

Lead Plated Exoskeleton. You do not suffer any limb conditions from Targeted Attacks and your limbs cannot be severed. Additionally, if your Power Armor has less than 6 levels of Decay, you are immune to Radiation. If your Power Armor has 6 to 9 levels of Decay, you have advantage on Radiation checks. If your Power Armor has 10 levels of Decay, it offers no protection against Radiation.

Oxygen Tank. You can breathe underwater, however you cannot swim and you sink at a rate of 100 ft. each round.

Atmospheric Seal. As long as your helmet is on, you are immune to any air-based hazards, such as toxic air, smoke, or airborne disease. If your Power Armor has more than 8 levels of Decay, you lose the benefit of this property.

Power Armor Special Properties

Heat Resistant. When wearing the Power Armor, you take twice as long to gain levels of Overheating and are resistant to fire damage.

Cold Resistant. When wearing the Power Armor, you take twice as long to gain levels of Hypothermia and are resistant to cold damage.

Industrial. While wearing the Power Armor, your Strength ability score is considered a 15 instead of a 12. Additionally, Carry Load increases by 50.

Recycling. While wearing this Power Armor, whenever you consume 8 oz of a liquid, it is converted into 4 oz of Purified Water. (2 drinks recycles into 1 Purified Water).

Intimidating. While wearing this Power Armor, you have disadvantage on all Charisma ability and skill checks except for Intimidation skill checks, which you have advantage on.

Clunky. While wearing this Power Armor, you have disadvantage on any non-combat Agility ability or skill checks. Attack rolls are unaffected.

Prototype. Whenever this Power Armor gains a level of Decay, it gains twice as many.
