fields.effect: The weapon’s damage is 1d4+2 and you do not add the Agility modifier. If the attack damages a target’s HP, the target takes 1 level of Fatigue. Additionally, if the attack brings a target to 0 HP, the target instead heals 1 HP and gains the Unconscious condition, unless the attack was a Targeted Attack to the Head or Eyes.
The weapon’s range modifiers are tripled and it gains the Accurate and Destructive properties, and it loses the Low Penetration property. However, it also loses its Spread and Powerful properties.
The weapon gains the same effects as the Slug ammo type. Additionally, the damage type is now both ballistic and electricity.

fields.name: Bulk (x0.5)
fields.effect: The weapon’s damage is reduced by 3, however it gains the Durable property.
The weapon’s damage is increased by 1 and ignores 1 DT.
The weapon’s damage is increased by 2 and ignores 2 DT. However, the weapon gains the Breakable property.
The weapon’s damage is increased by 4 and ignores 4 DT. However, the weapon gains the Breakable property, and after every 3rd attack, the weapon gains a level of Decay.
The target gains the effects of the Stimpak you load the syringe with.
The target gains the effect of the chem you load the syringe with.
The target gains the Poisoned condition for 3 turns and takes 1d6 poison damage at the start of each of those 3 turns.
The target’s DT is reduced by 3 for 1 minute.
The target becomes Frightened for 3 rounds.
The target spends all its AP on its next turn to attack the nearest creature.
The target gains 1 level of Bleeding.
The target gains the Slowed condition for 2 rounds.
The target gains the Deafened condition for 3 rounds.
The target gains the Blinded condition for 3 rounds.
The target can no longer see any creatures beyond 30 ft. of them for 1 minute.

If the target’s Endurance is 4 or lower, they fall Unconscious for 1 hour. Otherwise, the target gains the Dazed condition for 3 turns and falls Unconscious at the end of their 3rd turn. A creature can remove this condition by using a chem with the Stimulant property.

entity.name: Empty Syringe
entity.effect: This syringe has no additional effects.

entity.name: Diseased Dart
entity.effect: The target must make a Disease check.

entity.name: Bloatfly Larva
entity.effect: The target must make a DC 10 Endurance check. If they fail, the larva infests their body. They will take 1d8 poison damage at the start of each of their turns, and after 5 turns, they will take 2d10 damage as a Bloatfly spawns on their spot. If the target dies before this point, a Bloatfly will spawn from their corpse once the target would’ve reached 5 turns.

entity.name: Teeth (x0.2)
entity.effect: If the attack damages a target’s HP, they must make a Disease check. Damage is 1d4 and you do not add the Agility modifier.

entity.name: Homemade Fuel (x0.5)
entity.effect: The weapon gains the Breakable property, and after every 2nd attack, the weapon gains a level of Decay.

entity.name: Optimized Fuel (x2)
entity.effect: The weapon’s damage is increased by 2 and ignores 1 DT. However, after every 3rd attack, the weapon gains a level of Decay.

entity.name: Low Yield (x0.75)
entity.effect: The weapon’s number of damage dice is decreased by 4 and its explosive radius is decreased by 10 ft.. However, the range is increased by 50 ft..

entity.name: Big Kid (x3)
entity.effect: The weapon’s number of damage dice is increased by 4 and its explosive radius is increased by 10 ft.. However, the range is decreased by 50 ft..

entity.name: Tiny Tots (x3)
entity.effect: The weapon now makes 3 attacks for 1 round. However, the number of damage dice is decreased by 8 and the explosive radius is decreased by 20 ft..

entity.name: High Velocity (x4)
entity.effect: The weapon loses the Slow property.

entity.name: Hive (x5)
entity.effect: The weapon now makes 3 attacks for 1 round. However, the number of damage dice is decreased by 4 and the explosive radius is reduced by 5 ft..

entity.name: High Explosive (x4)
entity.effect: The weapon’s number of damage dice is increased by 2, and its explosive radius is increased by 10 ft..

entity.name: Plasma (x4)
entity.effect: The weapon does an extra 2d8 plasma damage and its range is increased by 5 ft., however its explosive damage is reduced to 1d8.

entity.name: Pulse (x4)
entity.effect: The weapon does an extra 2d8 electricity damage and its range is increased by 10 ft., however its explosive damage is reduced to 1d4.

entity.name: Incendiary (x5)
entity.effect: The weapon gains the Incendiary property, however its explosive damage is reduced to 1d8.

entity.name: Flechette (x2)
entity.effect: The weapon gains the Spread property, however its short & long range modifiers are decreased by 2.

entity.name: Barbed (x2)
entity.effect: When you deal damage to a target’s HP, they gain a level of Bleeding.

entity.name: Cryo (x5)
entity.effect: Targets hit by the weapon gain the Slowed condition until the end of their next turn.

entity.name: Explosive (x10)
entity.effect: When hit, any creature or object within 5 ft. of the target, including the target, takes 3d6 explosive damage. The target falls prone if their Strength ability score is lower than 10. The arrow/bolt is destroyed and cannot be retrieved.

entity.name: Firework (x8)
entity.effect: When hit, any creature or object within 5 ft. of the target takes 2d6 explosive damage, and any creature within 10 ft. of the target gains the Blinded condition for 2 turns. The arrow/bolt is destroyed and cannot be retrieved.

entity.name: Flaming (x3)
entity.effect: When you deal damage to a target’s HP with a weapon that has this property, they gain the Burning condition. If an attack with this weapon misses, the projectile may land nearby and start a fire (up to Overseer’s discretion). Any flammable objects hit by a weapon that has this property will immediately burst into flames. The arrow/bolt is destroyed and cannot be retrieved.

entity.name: Plasma (x10)
entity.effect: The arrow/bolt deals an additional 1d8 plasma damage.

entity.name: Poison (x4)
entity.effect: When you deal damage to a target’s HP, they gain the Poisoned condition for 3 turns.

entity.name: EMP (x8)
entity.effect: The arrow/bolt deals an additional 1d8 electricity damage. If the target is wearing Power Armor, they lose 50 Operational AP. The arrow is destroyed and cannot be retrieved.

entity.name: Concussive (x10)
entity.effect: The arrow/bolt releases a concussive blast on impact with a target, dealing 2d6 sonic damage and knocking the target back 5 ft.. The arrow is destroyed and cannot be retrieved.

entity.name: Flash (x3)
entity.effect: Upon hitting a target, the arrow/bolt releases a flash of Bright Light. Any creature in a radius of 10 ft. gains the Blinded condition for 1 round.

entity.name: Rebar Bolt (x5)
entity.effect: The weapon gains an additional damage die, however it now costs +1 AP to shoot.

entity.name: Shell Tipped (x3)
entity.effect: The arrow is tipped with a 12 gauge shotgun shell and deals an additional 2d6 ballistic damage. The arrow is destroyed and cannot be retrieved.

entity.name: Barbed (x5)
entity.effect: When you deal damage to a target’s HP, they gain a level of Bleeding. The arrow is destroyed and cannot be retrieved.

entity.name: Dart (x3)
entity.effect: The arrow can be loaded with one of the Syringer’s syringes, inflicting the condition. The arrow is destroyed and cannot be retrieved.

entity.name: Net (x8)
entity.effect: Upon hitting a target, the arrow releases a net that envelopes them, and the target is Restrained. The target must spend 6 AP to make a DC 12 Agility ability check to free themselves from the net. On a success, they escape the net and lose the Restrained condition. On a failure, they remain ensnared in the net.

fields.description: A brand of highly advanced steroids that increase strength, reflexes, and endurance, ingested via tablets.
Buffout tablets chemically mixed with Jet to produce the effects of both.
Buffout tablets chemically mixed with Mentats to produce the effects of both.
A light tranquilizer delivered via syringe. It carries a high enough dosage to cause a boost of some survival senses that are ordinarily dulled by reasoning.
An inhaled tobacco product that was widely popular before the war, and remains one of the most common and cheapest chems available.

fields.name: Coyote Tobacco Chew
fields.description: A leaf harvested from a coyote tobacco plant, when chewed it causes invigoration and aids in focus.
An injected chemical popular amongst beatniks and intellectuals that heightens cognitive faculties, along with a hyperfocus that makes interactions awkward.
A mild hallucinogenic chem delivered via pills, popular for providing an escape from reality. It was used both recreationally and medically for patients suffering from PTSD and similar conditions.
A derivative of Psycho, except with extremely heightened effects. Known for inducing a sense of invulnerability and intense, furious anger.
A soda bottle with multiple chemical vials feeding into it used to dull the pain of severe injuries.
A highly addictive chem delivered via a red inhaler, stimulating the central nervous system and triggering a rush of energy.

fields.name: Jet Fuel
fields.description: A derivative of Jet, infused with actual flamer fuel to produce a stronger high.
A heightened derivative of Jet, combining the invigorating effects of Jet and Nuka Cola to produce an immense burst of energy.
An experimental derivative of Jet designed to allow ghouls to experience the effects, accomplished by doubling the effects for everyone else.
A brand of morphine delivered via syringe to provide pain relief. Though it’s intended to be used medically, it found widespread recreational use.
Strong nootropics ingested via chalky tablets that increase cognitive processes and memory recall.
A flavor of Mentats designed to intensify the cognitive increase, at the cost of social awkwardness.
A flavor of Mentats designed to increase one’s confidence in social situations.
A flavor of Mentats designed to amplify one’s ability to focus on specific tasks.
A derivative of Psycho mixed with Nuka Cola to provide a burst of energy.
A chem used by the military, consisting of mysterious chemicals injected via syringe to induce rage and fearlessness in soldiers.

fields.name: Psycho Buff
fields.description: A derivative of Psycho mixed with crushed Buffout tablets to provide the effects of both.

fields.name: Psycho Jet
fields.description: A derivative of Psycho mixed with Jet to provide the effects of both.

A program that runs through a robot’s cache and removes unnecessary data, allowing for faster processing speed.

Crafting Programs (Science DC, time to program):
Cache Clearer: DC +2, 10 minutes
Coolant Rerouter: DC +8, 2 hours
Predictive Chatbot: DC +5, 1 hour
Data Scrubber: DC +3, 30 minutes
EISENHOWER PROTOCOL: DC +10, 2 hours
Incoming Projectile Predictor: DC +3, 30 minutes
Military Auto-Tank AI Upload: DC +8, 2 hours
Military Turret Operating System: DC +8, 2 hours
Overclock Hardware: DC +3, 30 minutes
Overclock Hardware v2.0: DC +5, 1 hour
Servo Override: DC +3, 30 minutes
A program that reroutes coolant from other parts of the system to the CPU to increase processing speeds.
A program that scrubs unneeded data input, allowing more important data to take priority for processing.
A military-grade program that deactivates all but the basic spatial awareness processes in order to maximize combat efficiency.
A program that analyzes incoming projectiles in real time to predict the impact site, and then reroute resources to lessen the damage.
A military-grade program that redirects resources to combat and damage mitigation protocols.
A military-grade program that temporarily replaces the existing operating system with one designed for combat, at the cost of anything else.
A program that increases power input to all systems for a short period of time.
A program that redirects the power supply to critical systems.
A program that overrides the limits on servo hardware, allowing greater stress capacity.

entity.name: Steady
entity.description: A powerful chem delivered via a makeshift inhaler made with a bottle and a hose, often used by snipers to steady their aim - thus the name.

entity.name: Slasher
entity.description: A derivative of Psycho mixed with Med-X to produce the effects of both.

entity.name: Turbo
entity.description: A hairspray canister with a Jet inhaler strapped to it, creating a cocktail of chemicals inside that induces a sense of slow motion when sprayed into one’s mouth.

entity.name: Voca-Stim
entity.description: Small tablets developed to produce confidence in social situations when consumed.

entity.name: X-Cell
entity.properties: Invigorating, Anesthetic, Anabolic, Articulative, Neuro-Stimulant, Hallucinogenic
entity.description: A prototype general performance enhancement chem, delivered via inhaler, that was widespread on the pre-war black market.

entity.name: Predictive Chatbot
entity.description: A program that analyzes conversations in real time to provide the optimal response for a given situation.

fields.description:
An experimental inhaled medicine that removes the physical and psychological effects of addiction, though at the cost of side effects such as nausea and dehydration.

Consumed with 4 AP. You are cured of all addictions, however you gain three levels of Dehydration, Hunger, and Exhaustion.

A pill of antibiotic medication used to remedy diseases and provide additional protection against infection.

Consumed with 3 AP. Can be used to cure certain diseases. Additionally, you have advantage on any Disease checks for the next 3 hours.

A natural antidote to most poisons produced by venomous animals, both for nullifying existing effects and preparing for future dangers.

Consumed with 5 AP. You are resistant to Poison damage to your HP for the next 6 hours and remove the Poisoned condition if you have it.

A small pill that increases the amount of light absorbed by the eyes, effectively giving the user night vision in dark environments.

Consumed with 3 AP. You gain Night Vision for 3 hours.

A large carry bag full of medical supplies, often used by doctors and field medics to provide emergency aid. The tools within are able to fix more severe injuries than smaller medical kits.

Medical kit with 3 uses for one of the following actions: Tourniquet. Spend 6 AP and remove two levels of Bleeding. Pain Killer. Spend 6 AP to heal a Dying creature to 1 HP. Stitch Wounds. Spend 10 minutes to heal a creature with a number of HP equal to double their Healing Rate + your Medicine skill modifier. Set Bone. Spend 10 minutes to remove a creature’s Broken Arm or Broken Leg condition.

A commercial tablet medicine designed to combat the negative effects of addiction, at the cost of nausea and fatigue.

Consumed with 4 AP. You cure one addiction, however you gain a level of Dehydration, Hunger and Exhaustion.

A small, portable box full of medical supplies, often used by doctors and field medics to provide emergency aid.

Medical kit with 1 use for one of the following actions: Tourniquet. Spend 6 AP and remove two levels of Bleeding. Pain Killer. Spend 6 AP to heal a Dying creature to 1 HP. Stitch Wounds. Spend 10 minutes to heal a creature with a number of HP equal to double their Healing Rate + your Medicine skill modifier.

A natural remedy of crushed herbs that dulls pain and heals minor wounds.

Consumed with 6 AP. For 3 rounds, you heal a number of HP equal to half your Healing Rate at the start of your turn. Does not work on Ghouls, Robots or Gen-2 Synths.

A chemical solution that bonds with radioactive particles and removes them from the user's system, injected intravenously. These particles are flushed out with waste water.

Spend 15 minutes to remove two levels of Radiation but gain one level of Dehydration.

Rad-Away that has been diluted, lowering its effectiveness.

Spend 15 minutes to remove one level of Radiation but gain one level of Dehydration.

A medical pill that works to bolster the body’s natural resistance to radiation.

Consumed with 3 AP. Your Radiation DC decreases by 2 for the next 3 hours. Effect can stack 3 times.

A hand-held syringe filled with coagulants and stimulants to boost the body’s natural regenerative functions.

Consumed with 4 AP. You heal a number of HP equal to your Healing Rate. If you are a Ghoul, you heal half your Healing Rate.

A Stimpak that has been diluted, lowering its effectiveness.

Consumed with 4 AP. You heal a number of HP equal to half your Healing Rate. If you are a Ghoul, you heal a number equal to quarter of your Healing Rate.

A more powerful version of a Stimpak, fitted with a leather belt that is strapped onto the arm when injecting the syringe.

Consumed with 4 AP. You heal a number of HP equal to double your Healing Rate. If you are a Ghoul, you heal a number equal to your Healing Rate.

A Stimpak equipped with tech that monitors the vital signs of the user and injects itself automatically when enough damage is detected.

When your HP is equal to half or lower than your maximum HP, the Auto-Inject Stimpak is consumed and gives you the effects of a Stimpak.

A Super Stimpak equipped with tech that monitors the vital signs of the user and injects itself automatically when enough damage is detected.

When your HP is equal to half or lower than your maximum HP, the Auto-Inject Stimpak is consumed and gives you the effects of a Super Stimpak.

entity.name: Robot Repair Kit 1.0
entity.description:
A set of specialized tools designed to repair minor damage to robots.

Can only be used by robots. Consumed with 4 AP. Robots heal a number of HP equal to half their Healing Rate.

entity.name: Robot Repair Kit 2.0
entity.description:
A set of specialized tools designed to repair significant damage to robots.

Can only be used by robots. Consumed with 4 AP. Robots heal a number of HP equal to their Healing Rate.

entity.name: Emergency Robot Repair Kit
entity.description:
A set of specialized tools designed to repair severe damage to robots.

Can only be used by robots. Consumed with 4 AP. Robots heal a number of HP equal to double their Healing Rate.

entity.name: Vial
entity.description:
A vial of unknown chemicals that reacts with the physiology of ghouls in a unique way, lessening the cognitive effects of feralization.

Consumed with 3 AP. Ghouls remove 1 Feral Level. Non-Ghouls gain no effects.

entity.name: Alien Biogel
entity.description:
A mysterious blue gel created by aliens that interacts with human physiology in an interesting and unique way.

Consumed with 4 AP. You heal a number of HP equal to half your Healing Rate. Additionally, a random chem effect is applied to you for 1 hour. Roll a d12 to determine the effect using the Chem Properties table, not counting Super Stimulant and Hyperstimulant. You can reroll a number of times equal to your Luck ability modifier.

fields.description: A pre-packed, highly processed box of classic mac & cheese created by BlamCo to provide an easy instant meal for families.
A can of Doghouse brand beef stew meant for dogs, but still consumable by a desperate survivor.
A tin of pre-sliced, precooked, preserved meat that was very popular in the war for its nearly unlimited shelf life. After the war, it’s an easy and common source for a good, if bland, meal.
A pre-war box of sliced apples, stuffed with enough preservatives to keep them edible for centuries.
A box of frosted snack cakes that retain their tastiness even centuries after the war, though they tend to be a bit stale.
A box of freeze-dried powdered mashed potatoes. They taste better with added water, but eating it out of the box is also an option.
A nutritious meal held in a tin can composed of beans stewed in a tomato sauce with chunks of pork belly cured and cooked in hickory smoke. Perfect for the hungry prospector.
A small box of packaged salted or flavored potato chips, good for a quick snack.
A sealed pre-packaged meal consisting of ground beef steak, mixed with various ingredients, alongside gravy.
A box of the popular pre-war cereal, with sugar coated wheat cereals shaped like nuclear bombs, often served with milk.
A box of hard-boiled eggs that have been shelled, cut in half and filled with yolk mixed with other ingredients such as mayonnaise and mustard. Kept fresh and edible through preservatives.
A spiny fruit harvested from the agave plant.
A common fruit that grows on apple trees, known for its distinct shape and red color.
A fruit harvested from the banana yucca plant.
A fruit with a high water content harvested from desert cacti.
A collection of dark purple berries that grow on bushes.
A cluster of red, semi-aquatic leaves found on bloodleaf plants in lakes, rivers, and other bodies of water.

fields.name: Brain Fungus
fields.description: A fungus that grows in dark, damp places, known for its pale coloration and brain-like texture, thus the name.
A long, orange root vegetable commonly grown as a crop.
A bioluminescent fungus often found growing in caves. It can glow a wide variety of colors, most commonly green.
An excellent source of nutrients as well as an easy-to-grow crop. Past its use as sustenance, surplus corn can be refined into biodiesel.
A bright red edible berry that can be picked from a cranberry plant.
A large, pale-orange, edible fruit which is treated as a vegetable for culinary purposes, known for its tough interior.
A large, green fruit that grows on a vine.
A mutated species of apple that can be found all across the wasteland, characterized by its rugged, purple exterior.
An oddly shaped green fruit that grows from pear trees.
A starchy, brown vegetable that grows underground via a root plant. It is still grown in some places in the wasteland.

fields.name: Prickly Pear Fruit
fields.description: A fruit harvested from the prickly pear cactus, often found in the desert.
A golden-colored, grass-like grain widely cultivated across the wasteland, often used as a replacement for wheat.

fields.name: Silt Bean
fields.description: Red pods of legumes that grow in the wilderness on silt bean plant vines.
Small, purple berries harvested from water-grown tarberry plants.
A mutated hybrid of a potato and a tomato plant, resulting in an edible fruit with the stem and skin of a tomato, but the brownish flesh of a potato.
A root commonly found in the desert around rocky areas, known for its healing properties.

A large glass bottle containing a green, highly alcoholic beverage distilled from a fermented mash containing wormwood, fennel, aniseed, and other herbs.
A novelty drink mixer shaped like a rocket ship containing a lightly glowing green beverage, known for its energizing qualities.
A glass bottle containing a dark brown beverage made from a variety of cereal grains, such as barley, wheat, maize, and rice.
A dark brown beverage with a high caffeine content, popular as a morning or late night drink to stave off sleepiness.
Coffee brewed by boiling roasted coyote tobacco chew and honey mesquite pods. Not as tasty, but good in a survival scenario.
A powerful alcoholic mixture brewed after the war, made by mixing various post-war produce and drinks.

fields.name: Dirty Water
fields.description: A bottle of contaminated and irradiated water. Not great, but better than dying of dehydration.
A high-proof liquor contained in a large jug, typically brewed in makeshift set-ups by those trying to avoid attention.

fields.name: Nuka Cola
fields.description: The most popular drink in the pre-war US, whether in its rocket bottle or standard cola bottle. Known for its high sugar and caffeine content, as well as its unique radioactive property, this soft drink can be found anywhere in the wasteland.

fields.name: Nuka Cola Cherry
fields.description: A cherry-flavored Nuka Cola, notable for its light red color.

fields.name: Nuka Cola Quantum
fields.description: An experimental and very rare variant of Nuka Cola, distinguished by its bright blue glow and unique design. It only saw a limited release before the war.

fields.name: Purified Water
fields.description: A bottle of clean water, free of any contamination. Often found as pre-war emergency drinking water containers.
A strong liquor with a notable dark red color, served in a variety of bottles.
A variant of whiskey, typically contained in a tall bottle.
A root beer soft drink popular in the Southwest, known for its distinctive design on its bottles and great taste.
A distilled alcoholic beverage contained in a rectangular bottle, typically imported from the Soviet Union.
Water mixed with various fermented fruits found in the wasteland to create a mock version of whiskey.
A distilled alcoholic beverage made from fermented grain mash, known for its distinctive orange coloring.
A cheap and disgusting alternative to proper wine, brewed with makeshift fermented fruits. Doesn’t taste great, but it’s cheap.
Wine brewed over a long period of time using materials found in the wasteland. Not as good as pure wine, but it tastes fine enough.
An alcoholic beverage made from the fermentation of grape juice, often considered to be a high class alcoholic drink.

entity.name: Bubblegum
entity.description: A confectionary treat that comes in a variety of packages. It offers little to no caloric value, but it is quite tasty.

entity.name: Cotton Candy Bites
entity.description: A box of candies that taste just like cotton candy, lovely bite sized fun!

entity.name: Funnel Cake
entity.description: A pre-packaged box of the beloved surgery carnival and fair food.

entity.name: MRE
entity.description: A highly nutritious field ration used by the pre-war military. Meals were packed into plastic packages, ready to be warmed up with chemical heating pouches.

entity.name: Noodles
entity.description: A bowl of noodles, perfect for a good meal.

entity.name: Perfectly Preserved Pie
entity.description: Pre-war pies that have been preserved in Port-A-Diners for centuries, though they are notoriously hard to come by.

entity.name: Sugar
entity.description: A small canister of sugar. Not much of a meal, but it could be good for cooking.

entity.name: Aster
entity.description: A purple mutated flower, though its once vibrant color has become more muted.

entity.name: Honey
entity.description: A sweet food substance produced by honey bees in forests, often harvested from honeycombs and hives.

entity.name: Firecracker Berries
entity.description: Vibrant red berries that glow in the dark, known for its volatile plant that explodes like a firecracker when disturbed.

entity.name: Jalapeno Pepper
entity.description: A chilli pepper pod harvested from jalapeno plants, known for its spicy flavor.

entity.name: Lure Weed
entity.description: A glowing plant that normally floats at the top of ponds. It bears resemblance to the lure of an angler, which the creature uses to ambush prey.

entity.name: Megasloth Mushrooms
entity.description: A mushroom which has grown on the back of a megasloth over time.

entity.name: Pinyon Nuts
entity.description: A handful of nuts that grow from the pinyon tree. Not very filling, but a decent enough snack.

entity.name: Punga Fruit
entity.description: A fruit that grows in warm, moist swamps from punga plants, highly valued for its ability to remove radiation from the system.

entity.name: Spore Carrier Sap
entity.description: A sticky, sap-like substance harvested from spore carriers.

entity.name: Spore Plant Pods
entity.description: A large seed pod harvested from the mutated spore plant.

entity.name: Brahmin Milk
entity.description: A bucket or bottle of milk taken from a brahmin, known for its ability to absorb radiation in the body.

entity.name: Lemonade
entity.description: Lemonade was a classic drink before the war, and it remains one now. Though, lemons going extinct means the recipe had to change a bit.

entity.name: Hard Lemonade
entity.description: Lemonade that has been spiked with alcohol.

entity.name: Nuka Cola Dark
entity.description: An alcoholic variant of Nuka Cola with a distinct dark brown bottle, advertised to adults before the war.

entity.name: Nuka Cola Quartz
entity.properties: Irradiated, Caffeinated, Pungent, Night Vision for 1 hour
entity.description: A rarer variant of Nuka Cola, known for its white glowing color and its unique capacity to provide the consumer a sort of night vision for a short period of time.

entity.name: Nuka Cola Victory
entity.description: A variant of Nuka Cola featuring a patriotic design and a bright red glowing beverage.

entity.name: Nuka Cola Wild
entity.description: A rustic, root-flavored variant of Nuka Cola, intended to compete with the regional Sunset Sarsaparilla.

entity.name: Nuka-Cola Orange
entity.description: An orange-flavored variant of Nuka Cola with a distinct orange color.

entity.name: Nuka-Grape
entity.description: A grape-flavored variant of Nuka Cola with a distinct purple color.

entity.name: Vim!
entity.description: A regional beverage from Bar Harbor, Maine, with a distinct taste due to its unique fermentation process. It’s rare to find these elsewhere in the wasteland, but it’s possible.

entity.name: Vim! Refresh
entity.description: A variant of Vim! known for its green color and lime-apple flavor.

entity.name: Vim! Quartz
entity.description: A variant of Vim! known for its glowing white color and its bubblegum flavor. The Vim Corporation got into hot water with Nuka Cola over copyright concerns with this drink.

entity.name: Vim! Captain’s Blend
entity.properties: Caffeinated, Pungent, Tasty, Charged While under the effect of this drink, sea creatures like Mirelurks do not see you as a hostile enemy until you directly attack them.
entity.description: An unreleased variant of Vim! with a distinctive glowing purple color and an odd lobster flavor. Strangely, sea creatures seem to be averse to attacking anyone who drinks this beverage.

fields.name: Bag (Backpack)
fields.description:
A leather, burlap, or cloth bag with straps or a sling to grant you more space to store items on you. While you wear a backpack, your Carry Load increases by 50.

If you wear more than one bag that has items stored in it, you are Encumbered unless your Strength or Endurance score is greater than or equal to 8.

fields.name: Bag (Range)
fields.description:
This single bag with one sling is longer to allow weapons to be stored in it with ease. You can store up to three weapons in the bag that have the Two Handed or Unwieldy property. If you do, each weapon's Load is halved.

If you wear more than one bag that has items stored in it, you are Encumbered unless your Strength or Endurance score is greater than or equal to 8.

This pocketed strap fits across any part of the body to allow for additional items to be carried. It is not considered a bag, allowing you to wear it and a backpack without becoming Encumbered. While you wear a bandolier your Carry Load increases by 25.

You can spend 3 AP to scatter these small metal spheres across a flat surface in a 5 ft. radius. Any creature who walks or runs through the area falls prone and takes 1d4 impact damage, unless the creature has a passive sense above 15 or has otherwise noticed the ball bearings; they must spend 2 AP for every 5 ft. of movement.

Removed on use. Can be picked back up by spending 10 minutes gathering them all together.

You can spend 6 AP to arm this bear trap in a 5 ft. area. If the trap is already triggered, you can reset it with 6 AP and a DC 15 Strength check. If a creature moves into the area, the trap triggers and they take 3d4 piercing damage to their hit points and the creature becomes grappled. You can disarm an untriggered bear trap with 6 AP and a DC 15 Crafting skill check. You can attempt to pry open a triggered bear trap with 6 AP and a DC 15 Strength ability check. If you are grappled by the bear trap when you attempt this ability check; you have disadvantage on the roll unless your Endurance ability score is 6 or greater. On a success, you open the bear trap and any creatures grappled by it are no longer grappled. On a failure, the trap clamps back down on the grappled creature and they take 1d4 piercing damage.

You can spend 3 AP to look through binoculars. While you look through them, your sight is magnified. You have advantage on any Perception ability checks relying on sight when viewing objects, creatures, or a location that are at least 100 ft. away.

You can spend 3 AP to scatter these small sharp objects across a flat surface in a 5 ft. radius. Any creature who walks or runs through the area takes 10 piercing damage (this damage is not subtracted by DT), unless the creature has a passive sense above 15 or has otherwise noticed the caltrops; they must spend 2 AP for every 5 feet of movement.

Removed on use. Can be picked back up by spending 10 minutes gathering them all together.

The metal canteen holds 32 oz. of liquid.

Can hold 4 uses of a singular Drink.

Outside of the typical, practical uses of a chain; if you are holding a chain while attempting to grapple or strangle another creature, you have advantage on your Strength ability rolls. Chains have 10 AC, 10 DT, 10 HP, and weakness to ballistic, laser, and plasma damage.

You can spend 6 AP on your turn to light this flare. This flare creates red Bright Light in a 30 ft. radius and red Dim Light for an additional 30 ft.. This light lasts for 1 hour.

Can be used as an Improvised Weapon. Deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage, 1d4 on crit. If lit, deals an additional 1d8 fire damage.

You can spend 1 AP while holding this flashlight to create Bright Light in a 20 ft. cone and Dim Light for an additional 20 ft.. The light lasts for 8 hours so long as you spend 6 AP to load an Energy Cell into the flashlight.

Can be used as an Improvised Weapon. Deals 1d4 bludgeoning damage, 1d4 on crit.

fields.name: Gas Mask
fields.description:
While you wear this mask, your Radiation DC decreases by 3 and your Passive Sense decreases by 2. Additionally, you have protection against toxic airborne hazards.

Does not count as Armor.
When you enter an Irradiated Zone, this device detects the level of radiation and you learn the Radiation Severity Score.
A metal hook that can be tied and attached to rope with 6 AP.

This large yellow suit is lined with layers of lead to provide the most protection from radiation without wearing power armor. Due to its bulky design; it takes 1 minute to don or doff, and you cannot wear armor over the suit. While you wear the hazmat suit, your Radiation DC decreases by 10 - the suit’s levels of Decay, any Rads you gained are halved (rounded down), and you are resistant to radiation damage. For every 5 points of damage you take to your HP while wearing a hazmat suit, it gains a level of Decay. To repair a level of Decay for a hazmat suit, the Crafting DC is 12 and requires x2 lead and x1 cloth.

Cannot be worn with other pieces of Armor or Power Armor.

This suit includes a geiger counter, an air purification system, impact absorption, further padding, and is topped with a bulbous helmet resembling a space suit. The suit requires power in order to operate. It can be powered for 6 hours before needing to be recharged with 3 Energy Cells. Recharging it costs 6 AP. Thanks to its automatic shrink fitting system, It takes 30 seconds to don or doff, however you cannot wear armor while wearing this suit. While you wear the powered hazmat suit your DT is increased by 3, you cannot gain levels of Radiation or Rads, and you are immune to radiation damage. For every 5 points of damage you take to your HP while wearing a powered hazmat suit, it gains a level of Decay. To repair a level of Decay for a powered hazmat suit, the Crafting DC is 15 and requires x2 lead, x1 leather, and x1 circuitry.

Cannot be worn with other pieces of Armor or Power Armor.

Rope can be used to tie items together, make a pulley system, climb, or tie someone up. If you are holding a rope while attempting to grapple or strangle another creature, you have advantage on your Strength ability rolls. Ropes have 10 AC, 2 DT, 5 HP, and weakness to ballistic, laser, plasma, fire, and slashing damage.

This nylon, cloth, or hide bag allows you to sleep even in the roughest terrain. You are insulated from the cold when in a sleeping bag.

When resting with a Sleeping Bag, any environment is Comfortable.

fields.name: Tent (One Person)
fields.description: This small tent provides shelter from outside sources, weather, and terrain.

fields.name: Tent (Two Person)
fields.description: This larger tent provides shelter from outside sources, weather, and terrain.

This leather pouch is fitted with a cap and nozzle and holds 64 oz. of liquid.

Can hold 8 uses of a singular Drink.

This plastic box filled with tools and mechanisms was used during the Great War to repair soldiers' weapons with ease. Although the tech used to create them has long since been forgotten, many are still found across the wasteland. You can spend 6 AP to insert any weapon into the repair kit. After 1 minute, the weapon is ejected and loses 2 levels of Decay. The weapon repair kit ceases function after it has been used a total of 3 times.

entity.name: Bag (Camping)
entity.description:
This large, heavy duty backpack has nylon strings made for tightening, a waist belt to help balance, many pockets, and an overhead compartment for larger storage. While you wear a camping backpack, your Carry Load increases by 100.

If you wear more than one bag that has items stored in it, you are Encumbered unless your Strength or Endurance score is greater than or equal to 8.

entity.name: Lantern
entity.description: You can spend 1 AP while holding this lantern to create Bright Light in a 20 ft. radius and Dim Light for an additional 20 ft.. The light lasts for 5 hours so long as you spend 6 AP to refuel the lantern with x1 Fuel Canister or x3 oil materials.

entity.name: Lockpick
entity.description: These metal tools allow you to pick locks with far more proficiency. When you make a Breach skill check to pick a lock, the DC is reduced by 5. After you use these lockpicks a total of 5 times, they break and cease function.

entity.name: Fire Extinguisher
entity.description:
You can spend 3 AP to spray CO2 foam over a 5 ft. area that’s within 10 ft. of you. Any flames in that area will be extinguished. The fire extinguisher can be used 5 times before it is empty.

Can be used as an Improvised Weapon. Deals 2d10 bludgeoning damage, x2 on crit. If it gains a level of Decay, it loses one of its uses.

entity.name: Handcuffs
entity.description: A pair of metal handcuffs for restraining people. With 6 AP, the handcuffs can be attached to a humanoid creature within 5 ft.. If the creature is unwilling, it must make an opposed Strength ability check. If the creature is prone or restrained, they have disadvantage. If the creature is incapacitated or unconscious, they cannot resist being handcuffed. Once handcuffed, a creature is unable to use their hands. They can attempt to break out with a DC 18 Strength ability check, or the handcuffs can be unlocked either with a key or a DC 14 Breach skill check. The handcuffs can also be broken off. Handcuffs have 10 AC, 12 DT, 12 HP, and a weakness to bludgeoning damage.

entity.name: Codac R9000 Camera
entity.description:
A camera featuring a large flash bulb, capable of taking high resolution, full color photographs. Photos are taken with 3 AP and use Camera Film, and the camera can take 12 photos before being “reloaded”. When taking a photo, the flashbulb goes off, illuminating the area with Bright Light for 60 ft.. If any creature is within 10 ft. of and facing the photographer when this happens, they gain the Blinded condition for 1 round.

Not considered a Weapon.

entity.name: ProSnap Deluxe Camera
entity.description:
A compact rangefinder camera featuring multiple different lens options. Photos are taken with 3 AP and use Camera Film, and the camera can take 6 photos before being “reloaded”. The different lenses can be swapped out for 3 AP and are listed as follows: 105mm Lens. While looking through the camera, you have advantage on any Perception ability checks relying on sight when viewing objects, creatures, or a location that are at least 50 ft. away. 200mm Lens. While looking through the camera, you have advantage on any Perception ability checks relying on sight when viewing objects, creatures, or a location that are at least 100 ft. away. Night Vision Lens. While looking through the camera, you have Night Vision for 50 ft.. Targeting Lens. While looking through the camera, it will detect any living targets within 50 ft. in front of you and highlight them for 1 round.

Not considered a Weapon.

entity.name: Camera Film
entity.description:
Camera film is a celluloid material used in conjunction with a chemical process after exposure to light to produce photographs.

Not considered Ammunition.

entity.name: Prosthetic Limb
entity.description:
A prosthetic limb that can be used to restore basic functionality to a missing body part, such as a foot, hand, leg, or arm. The negative modifier to your Strength and/or Agility ability scores is halved from -2 to -1, and the limb regains its basic functionality. With a prosthetic foot/leg, your maximum movement is now limited to 40 ft. instead of 20 ft.. With a prosthetic hand/arm, you can now use it to interact with the world and use weapons, but any action using the hand/arm costs an additional +1 AP to perform. When you take damage to your HP from a Targeted Attack to a prosthetic arm or leg, you take no damage but still suffer a limb condition, and the prosthetic limb gains a level of Decay. The limb breaks if it reaches 10 levels of Decay. One level of Decay can be repaired with x1 steel, x1 rubber and x1 plastic. Additionally, if the limb would get severed again, instead the prosthetic limb is broken off. You do not go into Shock or gain any levels of Bleeding.

Cannot be used if you take the Adaptive Reflexes or Groovy perks for a specific body part.

entity.name: Robotic Limb
entity.description:
An advanced prosthetic limb that can perfectly restore the functionality of a missing body part, such as a foot, hand, leg, or arm. The negative modifier to your Strength and/or Agility ability scores is removed completely, and your limb regains full functionality. With a robotic foot/leg, your maximum movement is no longer limited. With a robotic hand/arm, you can now use it to interact with the world and use weapons with no downside. When you take damage to your HP from a Targeted Attack to a robotic arm or leg, you take no damage but still suffer a limb condition, and the robotic limb gains a level of Decay. The limb breaks if it reaches 10 levels of Decay. One level of Decay can be repaired with x1 steel, x1 gear, and x1 circuitry. Additionally, if the limb would get severed again, instead the robotic limb is broken off. You do not go into Shock or gain any levels of Bleeding.

Cannot be used if you take the Adaptive Reflexes or Groovy perks for a specific body part.

fields.effect: A magazine reviewing and discussing military firearms, often including exclusive details about prototype weaponry.
fields.description: A magazine reviewing and discussing military firearms, often including exclusive details about prototype weaponry. Skill: Guns.

fields.effect: A magazine that is entirely devoted to energy weapons used by the military, including interviews with military personnel about advanced new energy weapon systems.
fields.description: A magazine that is entirely devoted to energy weapons used by the military, including interviews with military personnel about advanced new energy weapon systems. Skill: Energy Weapons.

fields.effect: A magazine that details how to create makeshift explosives, banned by the FBI for dangerous material. Despite this, it can still be found all across the wasteland.
fields.description: A magazine that details how to create makeshift explosives, banned by the FBI for dangerous material. Despite this, it can still be found all across the wasteland. Skill: Explosives.

fields.effect: A comic book magazine telling the adventures of knights performing outlandish feats of melee prowess against monstrous foes.
fields.description: A comic book magazine telling the adventures of knights performing outlandish feats of melee prowess against monstrous foes. Skill: Melee Weapons.

fields.effect: A magazine aimed at fans of boxing, with discussions on technique and equipment. The magazine often reviewed boxing matches and interviewed professional boxers and boxing coaches.
fields.description: A magazine aimed at fans of boxing, with discussions on technique and equipment. The magazine often reviewed boxing matches and interviewed professional boxers and boxing coaches. Skill: Unarmed.

fields.effect: A magazine that discusses advancements in the medical field, including new technologies, medicines, procedures, and techniques. Often includes interviews with highlighted doctors and physicians.
fields.description: A magazine that discusses advancements in the medical field, including new technologies, medicines, procedures, and techniques. Often includes interviews with highlighted doctors and physicians. Skill: Medicine.

fields.effect: A magazine aimed at locksports interested in the most recent advancements in security systems, and more importantly, how to get past them.
fields.description: A magazine aimed at locksports interested in the most recent advancements in security systems, and more importantly, how to get past them. Skill: Breach.

fields.effect: A magazine that is dedicated to the do-it-yourself repairmen, with advice ranging from basic repairs to advanced projects. The magazine also reviewed various tools and had general advice articles for the amateurs.
fields.description: A magazine that is dedicated to the do-it-yourself repairmen, with advice ranging from basic repairs to advanced projects. The magazine also reviewed various tools and had general advice articles for the amateurs. Skill: Crafting.

fields.effect: A comic book magazine following La Fantoma, a superheroine who is a master of stealth and infiltration.
fields.description: A comic book magazine following La Fantoma, a superheroine who is a master of stealth and infiltration. Skill: Sneak.

fields.effect: A camping and hunting magazine aimed towards the young adult male demographic. Despite it being meant for pre-war enthusiasts, the magazine offers legitimate survival tips that can be applied to life in the wasteland.
fields.description: A camping and hunting magazine aimed towards the young adult male demographic. Despite it being meant for pre-war enthusiasts, the magazine offers legitimate survival tips that can be applied to life in the wasteland. Skill: Survival.

fields.effect: A magazine focused on business that covered all things related to commerce, often covering sales tactics and tips for building a small business.
fields.description: A magazine focused on business that covered all things related to commerce, often covering sales tactics and tips for building a small business. Skill: Barter.

fields.effect: A comic book magazine telling terrifying stories of horrible monsters and scary scenarios.
fields.description: A comic book magazine telling terrifying stories of horrible monsters and scary scenarios. Skill: Intimidation.

fields.effect: A magazine geared toward those who lack social grace, advertising itself as a primer for social interaction. It offers advice and tips on making friends, going on dates, and finding a soul mate.
fields.description: A magazine geared toward those who lack social grace, advertising itself as a primer for social interaction. It offers advice and tips on making friends, going on dates, and finding a soul mate. Skill: Speech.

fields.effect: A magazine oriented around computer programming and science, focused on the latest in pre-war advancements in programming. Some articles offer neat tips and tricks for navigating standard RobCo terminals.
fields.description: A magazine oriented around computer programming and science, focused on the latest in pre-war advancements in programming. Some articles offer neat tips and tricks for navigating standard RobCo terminals. Skill: Science.
The most basic type of Pip-Boy, this model provides no other features.

This model features a heartbeat and electromagnetic sensor. You can spend 2 AP to activate this sensor to know the cardinal direction of any small or larger creatures within 60 ft. of you that aren’t covered by at least 1 ft. of lead or steel. Additionally, this model functions as a Geiger Counter, Flashlight, and can connect to nearby radio stations.
This model features a number of new and improved functions. This model functions as a Geiger Counter, Flashlight, and can connect to nearby radio stations.

A RobCo Stealth Boy 3001 personal stealth device. This technological, pre-war wonder generates a modulating field that transmits the reflected light from one side of an object to the other. You can spend 3 AP to activate a stealth boy, once you activate you become invisible for 1 minute (10 rounds) so long as you keep the stealth boy on your body. Once a stealth boy has been activated, it cannot be activated again.

fields.name: Two-Way Radio
fields.description: These small militaristic devices allow for long range communication. The radio can be used 100 times before running out of power and needing to be reloaded. It is powered with 1 Energy Cell. Reloading it costs 6 AP. You can spend 3 AP to activate one of the radios, when you activate it; any sound made within 5 ft. of the radio is transmitted to the other radio which can be heard out to a range of 5 ft.. If both radios are activated simultaneously, neither emit any sound.

fields.name: Electronic Lockpick (Mk2)
fields.description: While far more robust in its design, this item’s function is identical to a standard Electronic Lockpick except that it breaks after 3 uses instead of 1.

entity.name: Alien Epoxy
entity.description: This mysterious vial of blue goo appears to excel at repairing material damage on tools, weapons and armor. You can spend 6 AP to pour the goo onto a weapon, armor or tool. After 1 minute, it will lose 2 levels of Decay. This consumes the epoxy.

entity.name: Chinese Stealth Armor
entity.description:
A form-fitting black bodysuit fitted with specialized technology designed for Chinese spies before the war. When worn, you can spend 3 AP to become Invisible for 1 minute. Once you activate this ability, it must recharge for 1 hour before being used again. The Stealth Armor functions as ballistic armor and has 12 AC and 3 DT, however it cannot be modified. Once it reaches 5 levels of Decay, the cloaking function no longer works until it is repaired.

Cannot be worn with other pieces of Armor or Power Armor. Cannot be modified.

entity.name: Explosive Collar
entity.description:
An Explosive Collar is often used by slavers to keep their slaves under control, but can be found for a variety of other uses around the wasteland.. Whoever puts the slave collar onto another individual can determine the conditions under which the collar will detonate. Once armed, an explosive collar can be disarmed either by using the key that comes with the collar or by passing an Explosives check, DC 16. If the individual trying to disarm the collar succeeds, the collar is disarmed and can be removed safely. If the individual fails the check by less than 5, the collar is not disarmed. If the individual fails the check by more than 5, the collar detonates, kills the collared individual, and deals 2d8 explosive damage to the individual. If a collared individual attempts to disarm their own collar, they make the Explosives check with disadvantage, however you add your Luck modifier to the roll.

Does not count as Armor.

entity.name: Mutation Serum
entity.description: This mysterious serum modifies your genetic material to create a specific mutation. Upon using this serum, you gain 1 Mutation of your choice.

entity.name: Night Vision Goggles
entity.description:
You can equip the goggles with 6 AP. When worn, you can spend 1 AP to turn it on/off. When on, you gain 100 ft. of Night Vision. This lasts for 6 hours before needing to spend 6 AP to load a fresh Energy Cell into the goggles. If goggles you are wearing are activated and you are exposed to Bright Light, you effectively suffer the Blinded condition until the goggles are deactivated or removed, or you leave the area of the light source.

Does not count as Armor. For every level of Decay, the operational time is decreased by 1 hour (to a minimum of 1).

entity.name: Pip-Boy 3000 MK IV
entity.description: This model features a heartbeat and electromagnetic sensor. You can spend 2 AP to activate this sensor to know the cardinal direction of any small or larger creatures within 60 ft. of you that aren’t covered by at least 1 ft. of lead or steel. Additionally, this model functions as a Geiger Counter, Flashlight, and can connect to nearby radio stations.

entity.name: Psychic Nullifier
entity.description:
A special type of headwear designed to nullify psychic energies, both from outside and within. Often used by Psykers to give themselves a reprieve from the chronic pain that their abilities inflict them with, however it also has the added benefit of becoming immune to other psychic attacks. While wearing it, you are immune to psychic damage and psychic abilities from Psykers. When a Psyker wears it, they no longer suffer the doubled negative effects of Exhaustion, however they can no longer use their psychic abilities.

Does not count as Armor.

entity.name: Vault Suit
entity.description: This form fitting single piece rubber and cloth jumpsuit is outfitted with biometric sensors with a heat-dissipation gold strip and antenna for health monitoring. Any vault suit functions as Cloth armor with a rank 1 Lead Lined upgrade, rank 1 Reinforced upgrade, rank 1 Fitted upgrade, and rank 1 Sturdy upgrade.

entity.name: Y-17 Trauma Override Harness
entity.description:
A prototype armor developed by Big MT, designed to take over a wearer’s motor functions when it detects grievous injury and return the wearer to a set home point. If the armor doesn’t have a home point set, it will instead enter a combat mode to defend the wearer. This functionality continues even after the wearer is dead. The Trauma Harness functions as Metal Armor and has 12 AC. If you go below 25% your maximum HP, the armor will take over and you become Restrained. It will immediately begin moving to a set home point, unless it has no home point, in which case it will try to eliminate any hostiles it can see. Once activated, a Trauma Harness has 8 AP, 40 HP, and 20 SP. Any damage dealt to an activated Trauma Harness will not damage the wearer. This SP and HP resets once the Trauma Harness is deactivated. Once an activated Trauma Harness reaches 0 HP, it will cease functioning and the armor will gain 10 levels of Decay, breaking.

Cannot be worn with other pieces of Armor or Power Armor. Cannot be modified.

steps.title: Race
steps.description: Choose your Race. (p. 4)

steps.title: Race variant
steps.description: Robots must choose their type: Handy, Protectron, Robobrain, Assaultron, Securitron or Automatron. The other races can, if your Overseer allows it, start with a variant. Humans can take Gen-3 Synth together with another variant.

steps.title: Many Roads Walked: +2 to two skills
steps.description: Ancient Ghoul: two skills of your choice are increased by 2.

steps.title: S.P.E.C.I.A.L.
steps.description: Each ability score starts at 5, and you have 3 points to assign. You can decrease scores to gain more points. If your Race modifies any of your ability scores, add the modifiers before assigning any points. Ability modifiers are equal to your score − 5. Luck adds half its modifier (rounded down) to every skill; if it is negative, every skill gets −1.

steps.title: Background
steps.description: Choose your Background. You gain a +2 to three different skills listed in your chosen Background (p. 4), its trait and its starting equipment.

steps.title: Background skills
steps.description: Custom Background: choose the three skills that get +2. (p. 13) The other backgrounds already add their +2.

steps.title: Background trait
steps.description: Custom Background: choose the trait your background gives, any trait from the list. (p. 13)

steps.title: Trait
steps.description: You can optionally choose a second trait besides your background’s, and optionally modify it with Wild Wasteland (the "Wild Wasteland" versions). (p. 4, 26) Traits come before perks because some change how many perks you get.

steps.title: Skilled: +2 to one skill
steps.description: Skilled: choose the skill whose modifier increases by 2.

steps.title: Skilled (Wild Wasteland): +5 to one skill
steps.description: Skilled (Wild Wasteland): choose the skill whose modifier increases by 5.

steps.title: Recluse: +3 to five skills
steps.description: Recluse: instead of gaining a perk at 1st level, five different skill modifiers of your choice increase by 3.

steps.title: Talented: −3 to five skills
steps.description: Talented: you gain an extra perk at 1st level. However, five different skill modifiers of your choice decrease by 3.

steps.title: Perk
steps.description: Choose a Perk that you meet the requirements for. (p. 4)

steps.title: Protectron: built-in tool
steps.description: Protect and Serve: choose one tool or weapon built into one of your arms. (p. 10)

steps.title: Handy: first arm
steps.description: Incredible Multi-Talented Appliance: Handys are built with three special tools, one in each of three arms. Choose the tool or weapon for your first arm. (p. 9)

steps.title: Handy: second arm
steps.description: The book says Handys are built with three tools (and can have three Grippers), but then says "choose one tool or weapon". Choose a tool for your second arm, or none, as agreed with your GM. The same tool can be chosen again. (p. 9)

steps.title: Handy: third arm
steps.description: Same as the second arm: choose a tool for your third arm, or none, as agreed with your GM. (p. 9)

steps.title: Equipment
steps.description: Add any equipment you gained from your background (the version for your race), with its decay and armor already worn. Alternatively, you can choose to take no equipment and gain 850 caps. (p. 4) What is not an item of the game goes to "Other items".

items.title: Story and appearance
items.placeholder: Where you come from, what you look like, what you seek in the wasteland…

steps.title: New level
steps.text: Whenever you gain 1000 XP, you gain a level. HP and SP rise at odd levels (5 + your Endurance or Agility modifier) and already show above. You gain 1 perk point at every level except 5th, 9th, 13th, 17th, 21st, 25th and 29th, and skill points at those levels instead (3, 4 or 5 by Intelligence).

steps.title: Perk point
steps.if: level != 5 and level != 9 and level != 13 and level != 17 and level != 21 and level != 25 and level != 29
steps.description: When you gain a perk point, you can use it to increase one of your ability scores by 1 or you can choose a perk that you meet the requirements for. (p. 5)

options.label: Choose a perk
options.text: A perk whose requirements you meet. You gain its effects when you choose it.

steps.title: Perk
steps.if: (level != 5 and level != 9 and level != 13 and level != 17 and level != 21 and level != 25 and level != 29) and perk_use == 1

steps.title: Ability score
steps.if: (level != 5 and level != 9 and level != 13 and level != 17 and level != 21 and level != 25 and level != 29) and perk_use == 2
steps.description: Choose the ability score that goes up by 1.

steps.title: Skill points
steps.if: level == 5 or level == 9 or level == 13 or level == 17 or level == 21 or level == 25 or level == 29
steps.description: Each point you spend in a skill grants it a permanent +1. (p. 5)
